Name: Crantzer
Question: What was Baylan Skoll‘s objective in Ahsoka?
Answer: The shortest, most accurate answer is that we don’t know for sure. However, I do have a theory: We know for sure this has something to do with the Mortis gods (seeing that Baylan made his way to find their ancient statues, perhaps made by a forgotten civilization). However, I want to get one common theory out of the way: Baylan isn’t trying to become the Father. Anakin is the Chosen One. The Father said as much in the Clone Wars: You are the Chosen One. You have brought balance to this world. Stay on this path, and you will do it again for the galaxy. It was even proven through Anakin’s ability to tame literal embodiments of both the light and dark side of the force. At the point of Ahsoka, both the Father and Anakin were dead. And, given that Anakin seems to be very much in control of his force ghost and even able to travel to and from the World Between Worlds easily, I would argue that Anakin is now the Father. The Father knew Anakin would take his place since he was the Chosen One. Given that Anakin is now the Father, I don’t believe Baylan is going for the title of Father. And if he was, he wouldn’t last long trying to square up against the Chosen One. So what is Baylan looking for on Peridea? Well, we also know that the planet Peridea was the ancient world of the Nightsisters, who are evil witches incredibly infused with force. We also hear one of the Nightsister witches say that Thrawn’s arrival had “awakened” them. I have a theory that the Nightsisters are largely powered by the legendary force being Abeloth. Long story short, Abeloth (in legends) is perhaps the most powerful force being in Star Wars legends lore. She was originally a common mortal woman of unknown name whom The Father brought on Mortis and allowed her to become the mother for the Son and Daughter, eventually being called the Mother. However, in a desperate attempt to become immortal like her husband and two children, she disobeyed the Father’s will and drank from the Font of Power, that the Son from, and she bathed in the Pool of Knowledge like the Daughter. But this power corrupted her and consumed her, twisting her mind and her body, creating the entity known as Abeloth. This eventually forced the Father to banish Abeloth (seeing as she was too powerful to kill) So, what does this have to do with Peridea? Well, I believe that Abeloth may have been banished to that desolate planet and founded what is now seen as the Witches of Dathomir. She likely gave them a strong connection to the force that they have and is potentially the source of their power. She may even be alive on Peridea at that very time. The Nightsister witches’ note of Thrawn’s return “awakening” them perhaps also meant awakening Abeloth as well. So what does this have to do with Baylan? Well, we see Baylan constantly hearing “voices” leading him to “power never before seen”. And it’s only on Peridea that he hears this. This “voice” may be Abeloth, perhaps leading him to become her servant or heir. That kind of power, if left unstopped, could make Bylan the most powerful force being ever seen.

Name: Crantzer
Question: When Tywin was young, was he good with a sword?
Answer: Absolutely. While we aren’t shown his skill with the sword in the show or books, Tywin is certainly a decent swordsman at the very least. He was an anointed knight at the age of just 18, and he has been part of numerous victorious battles, including the War of the Ninepenny Kings and the Battle of Blackwater Bay. Tywin was also a very traditional leader. In order to boost morale, Tywin often participated in the heat of the battle and even sometimes lead the charge, as was the case in the sack of King’s Landing against Aegon Targaryen and in the Blackwater. It’s highly unlikely that a highborn man with his battle experience, formal training, and knack for tactics would be anything less than pretty damn good with a sword.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who do you think is the coolest looking Jedi and the coolest looking Sith?
Answer: My absolute favorite Jedi outfit would have to go to Ahsoka’s white outfit. There’s something about its simplicity that gives it such a nicer look. While Sidious’ Chancellor robes are a close second, the coolest Sith outfit for me personally has to go to Count Dooku.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How were Thor, Groot, and Rocket able to pass through the force field surrounding Wakanda during the battle in Wakanda?
Answer: The Bifrost broke through the shield. You have to understand, the Bifrost was meant to fast-travel anytime, anyplace in any condition. Anything and anyone in its place has always been demolished. This includes vibranium. Some will argue that Wakanda opened their shields to let Thanos’ army in—however, T’Challa only said to open a section of the northwest part of the shield. This did not include the top, where Thor and his crew came from.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What would have happened if Count Dooku had remained a Jedi Master and eventually became the Grand Master of the Jedi Order instead of turning to the dark side?
Answer: It wouldn’t change as much as you think. Dooku wasn’t a true apprentice for Palpatine. He was simply a pawn in the Emperor’s grand plan—a guy to be disposed of once his plans came to fruition. The Sith Lord makes this clear to Vader after the events of RoTS: So what use did Palpatine have for Dooku? Well, Dooku’s entire purpose was to be the leader of the Separatist movement—he was supposed to lead and progress the Clone Wars with the strings that Palpatine had been pulling since the beginning. Dooku was the perfect candidate to lead the opposition—he was a defector of the Order, he was politically savvy, and he was a powerful man from a prominent family. It’s no wonder why so many planets backed him. However, not having him by Palpatine’s side would not have been the end of the world. The Sith Lord preferred Dooku, but he wasn’t necessary. While another general-like person (likely Grievous) would not have done as fine a job as the Count, he’d still be an acceptable replacement.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Wakanda Tech more advanced than Thor Technology?
Answer: Absolutely not. Wakanda is certainly the most technologically advanced society on Earth, but far from being among the most advanced in the universe like Asgard is. The science that Asgard uses is so advanced that the only way Earth can see it is as magic. Whether it comes to having instantaneous intergalactic space travel, a floating island nation, medical technology centuries ahead of its time, near-impenetrable armor and weaponry, or incalculably impressive architecture, Asgard solidifies itself as not just being miles ahead technologically compared to Wakanda, but also being among the pinnacle of civilization & power across the entire universe.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What would actually happen to the Earth if half of all life was Thanos snapped?
Answer: It’d be far worse than you think. Endgame seems to severely undermine the effects of what would happen. Just imagine some of the absolutely devastating yet almost-certain scenarios: That formerly 1/2 remaining population could easily turn into 1/5 in a matter of hours. This severe loss of life would also disrupt global systems. The logistics collapse of the world causes us to be in shambles. Global import/export systems no longer have enough people to keep manufacturing regularly, or keep electricity going or even paying them. That loss of manufacturing leads to a shortage of everything, from basic toiletries to food. Retail workers may grab what they could unless they get killed or kill each other, and those able to take what they can hog everything and use it as a means to sell at a criminally-high markup to those who need it. Law and order is a thing of the past. In a week or so, every form of crime is no longer illegal because no one is there to enforce it—every man is for himself and his family. The weak fall prey to those with a desire for power. The missing show no signs of returning and the world has officially stopped being controlled by any group of people. We watch as day by day, centuries of progress is obliterated.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Do you think Steve Rogers told Peggy that he was a time traveler?
Answer: No. After witnessing Steve’s death in real time and then going back home depressed, Steve came to Peggy’s house with flowers and simply told her that he managed to survive crashing into ice and then somehow walked all the way to her house without anyone else knowing. Yes, obviously Steve told Peggy he was from the future! There was no other possible explanation for Steve to be alive, nor was there any way that he could simply keep that secret from her for the ~60 years they spent together.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why do the leaders of Hamas not live in Gaza?
Answer: Because they’re cowards and hypocrites. Hamas is simply like many other political parties—a group of people who claim to “fight for the people” when in reality it’s for the profit of those at the top. In 2007, Hamas seized power in Gaza by killing the Fatah rulers appointed by the Palestinian Authority. Since then, the leaders of Hamas have taken corruption to an entirely new level. Hamas controls everything in Gaza through the use of force. They torture and kill with impunity. They collect import duties on all goods entering Gaza and own monopolies that are in control of every facet of life in Gaza. Everyone in Gaza pays in one way or another to the rulers of Hamas. Hamas have openly stated that the people of Gaza are refugees and are the responsibility of the international community and that Hamas is only responsible for the members of Hamas. They have no plans to improve the living standards of the ordinary citizens in Gaza. The world pours money into Gaza on the grounds of humanitarian aid, and this aid funds terrorism and the pockets of the leaders of Hamas. Hamas never cared about the people of Gaza, and they never will. They undid most of the schools and hospitals that Israel built when Gaza was under them, and they even destroyed all of the water pipes to turn them into cheap rockets. This is the same group who attacks Israel in the goal of genocide, then claim that Israel is doing the genocide when they defend themselves.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In Game of Thrones, when Tywin appointed Tyrion as Master of Coin, was hoping that he would succeed or fail in this position?
Answer: He legitimately wanted him to do well. Tywin was many things—but a saboteur of his own House was never one of them. Tywin gave Tyrion the position of Mater of Coin as a reward for his successes in the Battle of the Blackwater, and because he knew Tyrion had the intelligence to perform such a task. That being said, Tywin did deliberately prevent Tyrion from getting the promotion he deserved. Look back at their conversation after the Battle of Blackwater Bay: Tyrion: I want is mine by right. Jaime is your eldest son, heir to your lands and titles. But he is a kingsguard—forbidden from marriage or inheritance. The day Jaime put on the white cloak, he gave up his claim to Casterly Rock. I am your son and lawful heir. Tywin: You want Casterly Rock? Tyrion: It is mine by right. Tywin: We’ll find you accommodations more suited to your name and as a reward for your accomplishments during the Battle of Blackwater Bay. And when the time is right, you’ll be given a position fit for your talents so that you can serve your family and protect our legacy. And if you serve faithfully, you will be rewarded with a suitable wife. But I would let myself be consumed by maggots before mocking the family name and making you heir to Casterly Rock. Tyrion: Why? Tywin: Why? You ask that!? You who killed your mother to come into the world? You are ill-made, spiteful little creature full of envy, and lust, and low-cunning. You’ll notice that while he did insult Tyrion, Tywin did admit Tyrion’s acts of heroism and his prestige, and he did acknowledge that he’d be “given a position fit for [his] talents”. That position was Master of Coin. So did Tywin want Tyrion to succeed? Yes, he was a valuable asset that could benefit the kingdom in that position. But did Tywin purposely give him a lesser position out of pure spite? Also yes.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How did Thanos know the Reality Stone was on Knowhere?
Answer: Thanos didn’t just attack numerous realms over the course of a few days on a whim. It’s no coincidence that the Mad Titan happened to attack just days after Odin’s passing and when Asgard was at its weakest. It’s also no coincidence that he knew that both the Mind and Time Stones were on Earth. Thanos had planned this for years—probably even centuries. He tracked and studied where nearly every stone (except the Soul Stone) was. This could likely also explain why he knew who Tony Stark was, seeing as the Mad Titan may have done his research on Earth. The Collector was a much more famous individual than Earth or Stark. Many planets throughout the universe (including Asgard) knew who he was. So it’s no surprise that Thanos found out that he has the Reality Stone—it was probably common knowledge.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Would Kit Fisto have survived order 66 if he was on the battlefield instead of fighting Palpatine?
Answer: It’s possible. Kit Fisto is criminally underrated. He was the Master of Form 1 (Shii-Cho), and easily in the top 10 most skilled duelists ever in the Order. Fisto even nearly killed Grievous—a guy so feared that even Mace Windu left the fight against him in a stalemate. We also know that Obi-Wan (the greatest defensive duelist in the Order’s history) thought very highly of Fisto, even describing him as a “better swordfighter”: Obi-Wan and Kit had been engaged for an hour now, each seeking holes in the other’s defense. Obi-Wan swiftly discovered that Kit was the better swordfighter, astonishingly aggressive and intuitive in comparison with Obi-Wan’s more measured style. But the Nautolan gave himself deliberate disadvantages, hampered himself in terms of balance, limited his speed, emphasized his nondominant side to force himself to full attention, the kind of full attention that can be best accessed only when life itself is at risk. To relax and feel the flow of the Force under such stress was the true road to mastery. (The Cestus Deception) Fisto is far more formidable than many people think, and it’s because of the only fight we seen him in that is in live-action. In the fight against Palpatine, Fisto was caught off guard—what he once thought as a sweet, old man came whipping toward him like a tornado in less than a second. The only reason Mace didn’t also fall immediately was because of the other Masters dying before him. If it came down to a fight against clones, the Nautolan Master should have no problem winning. He has been proven to be exceptional as a duelist, so it’s highly likely that he could take on some clones like Obi-Wan and Yoda did. However, if he was surrounded and unaware like Aayla Secura, perhaps he would not have survived.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why does Steve Rogers love Peggy so much?
Answer: That’s the wrong question to ask. Steve fell in love with Peggy because she was the only woman to truly love him for who he was. All his life, Steve admits he hasn’t had the best luck with women. Having someone that really understands him and acknowledges him—that ought to make anyone fall in love. The real question is how did Peggy, even 70 years after meeting Steve, continue to be in love with a guy she knew for just a few days? Surely, she should have her fair share of eligible bachelors!

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did Tywin Lannister have any respect for Tyrion, despite not liking him?
Answer: Oh, yes. Although he hated his guts, Tywin did acknowledge that Tyrion was a strong-willed and strategic individual. Smarter than his siblings, at least. Even toward the end of his life, Tyrion told Tywin that he wanted him dead his whole life, to which Tywin replied, “Yes. But you refused to die. I respect that, even admire it”. Tywin even gave Tyrion honorable positions. For example, he gave him the position of Hand of the King (the highest position he could bestow) while Tywin was gone to battle. And even when Tywin got back, he gave Tyrion the position of Master of Coin. Tywin knew that Tyrion was smart and valuable. So as much as he hated him, he did have respect for the imp.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why didn't Palpatine use Order 66 in the Battle of Geonosis?
Answer: He wouldn’t have become Emperor. Palpatine had two main goals as Chancellor: At the point of the Battle of Geonosis, the Jedi were still relatively trusted & respected within the Republic, and the Republic had no real reason to shift their government system. None of his ultimate plans had come to fruition at that point. Sure, executing Order 66 would have killed the Jedi on Geonosis—but it would cause the people to view him as evil, and it would never allow him to take control within the Senate. However, the Clone Wars changed everything. After the Clone Wars, the general public started viewing the Jedi as tyrants on their land—people who had no jurisdiction but their own. And because it was war, there were also a number of casualties by the hands of the Jedi. The Clone Wars also caused great disarray within the Senate. Chaos ensued across hundreds of planets, and the Galaxy desperately needed someone to unite them all. Palpatine waited for the perfect time to strike. It was only after orchestrating the Clone Wars and causing both of his goals to happen that Palpatine finally decided that it was the perfect time to enact Order 66. That way, everything he desired would come to pass, and he would be seen as the savior that helped end the war and unite the people. It was also perfect because just minutes earlier, Palpatine managed to bring Anakin into the fold as his apprentice.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Which movie would have been five minutes long if its characters had just been sensible in the first place?
Answer: Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith. Had Anakin had any sense in him, he’d have taken Dooku in for questioning. He was a valuable asset, because at the time the Jedi were already onto a potential master above Dooku, and so having him there would have helped them get closer to the truth. Of course, that’s all not to mention that had Anakin waited just a few more seconds, Dooku certainly would have ratted Palpatine out after he betrayed him. After all, the Sith Lord couldn’t do anything to him at that point—he was cuffed to a chair!

Name: Crantzer
Question: What would happen if Order 66 and Order 65 were used at the same time?
Answer: If you’re not aware, Order 65 stated that if a majority of the Senate declared that the Supreme Chancellor was unfit for duty, the Chancellor was to be arrested or, if necessary, killed. So, in the event that the Senate happen to execute Order 65 at the same time that Palpatine executes Order 66, the Jedi would be killed off but then Palpatine would be the next target. The entire clone force would be too much for even the Sith Lord to handle. So either he’d be arrested or he’d die. “Ah, dank ferrik…” So, who would take Palpatine’s place? Well, the line of succession after the Chancellor was the Vice Chair. Thus, the Vice Chair would become the new Chancellor of the Republic. During Palpatine’s administration, that would be Mas Amedda.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Dr. Erskine choose Steve Rogers?
Answer: Dr. Erskine explains this himself: The serum amplifies everything that is inside. Good becomes great, bad becomes worse. This is why you were chosen—because a strong man who has known power all his life may lose respect for that power, but a weak man knows the value of strength. And he knows compassion. Whatever happens tomorrow, you must promise me one thing: that you will stay who you are. Not a perfect soldier, but a good man. The serum was dangerous—not because of its health risks, per se, but because of what it turns someone into. A man can successfully hide his true heart from others. But with the serum, this innate nature is amplified and intensifies their true intentions. A very good example of this is John Walker.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why was there a lack of diversity in Black Panther?
Answer: Just curious: have you ever heard complaints of a lack of diversity in Captain America: The First Avenger? How about either of the two Thor movies? What about DC movies like The Dark Knight Rises? I’m going to guess that the answer is no. All of the movies listed have had an almost-complete white-only cast, with 2–3 people of color to make up for it. The same (but reversed) goes for Black Panther. Look, I could not care less about the new push for “diversity in Hollywood”. But this is why I have no problem with Black Panther’s cast, either. This view of forced diversity poses hypocrisy on both sides of the aisle: those in support of this kind of diversity are hypocritical if they want a black-dominant cast for Black Panther. On the flip side, many who are against this new wave of diversity will have no problem with predominantly white-movies, but then hate movies like Black Panther for being “racist against white people” for not including them. Black Panther’s cast is absolutely fine as it is—we don’t need a quota of white people in a movie about a fictional African nation. At the same time, we also don’t need a quota of any other people group in Hollywood. All we need is good acting (and these days, that is scarce).

Name: Crantzer
Question: How would Anakin's life have been different if he had stayed with Obi-Wan instead of leaving the Jedi Order and going to Mustafar?
Answer: Things would’ve turned out much better than you think. Remember what Mace told Anakin before he went to confront Palpatine: Both Skywalker and Windu had been on edge over each other for a long time. But Mace makes it clear that had Anakin passed the emotional trial necessary of keeping himself in check and being trustworthy, he and the rest of the Council would have enough confidence to trust him. If Anakin had not killed Windu but instead trusted his advice, he would have become what he always wanted to be—a Master. Anakin would eventually also realize that nothing was truly wrong with Padme, and hopefully he’d come to the understanding that his dreams were fabricated by the Sith Lord. With Padme safe and Anakin by her side, they would raise their kids (perhaps on Coruscant to also train them as Jedi). And no, I don’t think the Council would expel Anakin for having a family, because 1) they kinda already knew, 2) he helped destroy the Sith just moments ago, and 3) he was the Chosen One after all. Honestly, it’d be a very happy ending.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What would happen if after executing order 66 and the Jedi, Palpatine ordered the execution of every Senator?
Answer: It wouldn’t work. Order 66 was an Order embedded into each clone during their manufacturing. This was one of five we know of in canon: Order 4 - In the event of the Chancellor being incapacitated, the overall command shall fall to the vice chair of the Senate. Order 5 - In the event of the Chancellor being declared unfit, the Chief of Defense staff shall assume command. Order 37 - Capture of a single wanted individual through the mass arrest and threatened execution of a civilian population. Follow-up directives include scenarios for body disposal of civilian casualties and suppression of communications. Order 65 - Arrest or death of the Supreme Chancellor. Order 66 - Neutralization of all Jedi officers in the event that they act against the interests of the Republic. Order 66 simply called for the order of the killing of all Jedi in the event of a coup. This did not include every senator, nor was there any other Order in canon that called for the eradication of the Senate. Because of this, the clones would not recognize Palpatine’s authority on the matter of eliminating every Senator, because it wasn’t in their programming to do so.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who wins? Robert Baratheon in his prime, or Arthur Dayne wielding Dawn?
Answer: It’d be a tough fight, to say the least. Robert in his prime was an absolute unit. He was a war-hungry 6′5 giant with a hammer and an antlered helmet. The guy was feared all throughout the realm and won nearly every battle he fought. He’s also said to be quite fast for his size. However, Arthur Dayne was something else. Dayne was the greatest knight in the history of the realm. No one dared to question his skill, because he has managed on many occasion to take on unbeatable odds and those twice his size. His sword Dawn only elevated his power, seeing as it was forged through the metal of fallen star (giving it a similar, if not better quality than Valyrian steel). Let’s put this in perspective: Ser Barristan Selmy was noted to be the most powerful man alive at the time Game of Thrones takes place. He in his prime managed to kill Maelys the Monstrous (the last of the Blackfyres), a man known for his freakish size and strength. In his old age, Barristan also killed a dozen Sons of the Harpy. And mind you, he was unarmed, old, and had a longsword in close combat (a weapon notorious for being terrible for close combat). And yet still, Barristan is noted in the books of being slightly lower in skill than Dayne. Robert would give Dayne a run for his money. The Demon on the Trident’s speed and brute strength would prove difficult for the Sword of the Morning, but men his size is something Arthur has dealt with much in the past. In the end, the Targaryen warrior would manage to kill Robert after a tough fight. Arthur Dayne wins.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What were some lesser-known Jedi who survived Order 66?
Answer: While Cal Kestis, Luminara Unduli, and Eeth Koth are the obvious ones who survived Order 66, there is one who is often overlooked and more powerful than them all: Kirak Infil’a. Infil’a was an absolute unit, and shortly before Order 66 he had took the Barash Vow, living in a rural area. Vader was sent not only to hunt down the ex-Jedi, but also to take his Kyber Krystal to form his own lightsaber. However, that did not go as planned.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Wasn't order 66 justified? The Jedi did just try to launch a coup against Palpatine after all.
Answer: Yes, from a legal standpoint. There was no law explicitly banning the practicing of the Sith’s religion and/or rituals. And the reason is obvious—there was no reason to. The Sith had been believed to be extinct for millennia. This is a big reason why the Jedi took such a risk when they attacked Palpatine—they had no solid proof linking him to anything other than that he was a Sith Lord. This was, of course, banned in the Order’s own doctrine, but it was completely legal in the Republic. Of course, the actions of most Sith do eventually lead to illegal activities (as defined by the Republic). Murder and torture were something few Sith had any problem doing. However, the fact remains that Palpatine himself had no solid evidence against him of any of his illegal activity. This was, of course, the biggest reason why the entire Senate rallied behind Palpatine even after Order 66.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if Obi-Wan and Anakin’s roles were switched and Obi- Wan fell to the Dark Side instead?
Answer: Obi-Wan wouldn’t be Palpatine’s apprentice. Palpatine desired one thing from Anakin—his potential. He had the potential to become the most powerful Force user in history. And despite his critical injuries, Vader still became the most powerful being alive at the time. He was Sidious’ menacing executioner. Kenobi would not have had such a role. Though he was immensely powerful, he paled in comparison to the likes of Vader or Palpatine in their primes. Instead, Obi-Wan’s strong suit was in negotiations and diplomacy. He had done it for the Republic much, with great success in the past. It’s likely thus, that Palpatine would instead allow Kenobi to use his talents as a high-ranking Grand Admiral or Moff.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Can Thor defeat Dormammu?
Answer: In comics, yes. Thor’s absolute peak is as Rune King Thor. This version of Thor had the full power of the Odin Force and Norse runes, allowing him to become omnipotent, see all points in time, manipulate minds, and even warp reality. This version of Thor could definitely take on any version of comics Dormammu, because in the comics Dormammu is a lot less powerful than his MCU counterpart. In the MCU, Thor doesn’t stand a chance. Thor in the MCU is not even close to the power of Rune King Thor from the comics. Sure, he’s become quite powerful over time (particularly in Infinity War and Love & Thunder), but it’s still not even a fraction of a fraction of his true potential. Dormammu, on the other hand, is a multiversally-revered being of unparalleled power that can destroy realities with a thought. In fact, he was so powerful that the entire purpose of the Sorcerer Supreme and their Order was not even to subdue/kill Dormammu, but to just keep him from attacking. No version of MCU Thor could even touch this Dormammu.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if Hela had never been corrupted and was there to be a good big sister to Thor and Loki?
Answer: Things would’ve turned out much better for everyone. Without Hela turning into the vengeful, Hela would have ruled by Odin’s side and helped Asgard become solidified as the greatest power in the universe. With this, Odin would also make Hela the queen. She was the rightful heir since the beginning, after all. And because of this, the insolent fighting between Thor and Loki as to who had a better claim to the throne would cease. This sibling trio would have been the greatest power known to the universe. Had Hela been ruler, beings like Thanos or Ronan would never have stood a chance. Even if Odin died, she was simply too powerful to be messed with.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How did Stan Lee come up with Spider-Man?
Answer: Actually, Stan talks about this in a UCLA Graduation Speech: My publisher came to me and he said, “Stan, I want you to come up with another superhero”. So I [agreed] and went home, and I saw a fly crawling on the wall. I said, “If I can get a superhero that could stick to walls and crawl on em, man that would be cool!” So I had my hero, I had this power, his name. And then I figured just for fun, I’m gonna give him personal problems. Then I thought I’d make him a teenager, cause there were no teenage superheroes that I knew of at the time. [Then] I ran into my publisher’s office and told him. This was the reaction he gave me: “Stan, that is the worst idea I have ever heard. First of all, people hate spiders—so you can’t call him Spider-Man. You want him to be a teenager? Teenagers can only be sidekicks! And you want him to have personal problems? Stan, don’t you know what a superhero is? They don’t have personal problems!”. I left the office disappointed…I couldn’t get Spider-Man out of my system. So we were about to kill a magazine, so just to get it out of my system, I put Spider-Man in Amazing Fantasy, featured him on the cover, and forgot about it. A month later, all the sales figures came in. My publisher came racing into my office, “Stan! You remember that character we both loved so much, Spider-Man? Let’s do him as a series!”. If you have an idea that you genuinely think is good, don’t let some idiot talk you out of it.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who would win in a fight between Homelander and Superman?
Answer: Superman would have no trouble against Homelander. Homelander is, by far, the weakest Superman parody in Hollywood. In his own universe, he’s a big man and the cream of the crop—but when compared to his counterparts, he’s just a weak man with an even weaker ego. In terms of durability, Homelander is seen being hurt by some relatively minor hits. Meanwhile, Clark has taken impacts that send shockwaves—and we rarely ever see him bleed. There’s no question as to who’s more powerful.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Other than Odin, which Asgardian matches up to Thor in terms of strength?
Answer: That would be Bor. Being the father of the Allfather, Bor was an ancient and legendary figure. Bor was also prized for building and solidifying Asgard within the universe. During his life, Bor had been destroying monsters of the early universe across the Nine Realms like nothing. He was a beast, through and through. By pure power, Bor was bigger and stronger than both of his descendants Odin and Thor. The only way Thor even managed to stand a chance against him was by using the Odinforce.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Captain America vs agent 47 who has the better super soldier serum?
Answer: So, here’s the thing: Bucky put up a good fight against Cap numerous times, putting him around Steve’s level. This same Bucky (with the help of Falcon) struggled much more against John Walker. Whether or not you argue that Bucky was without morals against Cap but not Walker, that doesn’t negate the fact that John’s strength and power is something neither Bucky nor Steve has shown. Dr. Nagel’s super soldier serum (which is the one Walker takes) has already been noted to be “more optimal” the old one. And by the looks of it, it's by a considerable margin. While you could argue that Steve has more super soldier experience, Walker was still a very skilled soldier who spent years being one of the best fighters in the military, even before he had the serum. He is a formidable foe. So yes, I’d say Walker has a serum that makes him stronger than Steve.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who would win between Dormamu vs Surtur?
Answer: Let me get this straight: you’re pitting a multi-dimensional being of unparalleled power and can control reality…against a fire guy? My money’s on the former.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If Windu brought more Jedi with him, would they have defeated Sidious?
Answer: Oh, yes. In fact, all it would take is one more Jedi: Plo Koon. Plo is a criminally underrated Jedi who was highly skilled, both with a saber and in the Force. He has taken on some very high-level threats (like Ventress) on occasion and won every battle we’ve seen him in. He was also a legendary star pilot, being second only to Anakin Skywalker. In the game The Clone Wars: Lightsaber Duels, it’s even mentioned by Skywalker that Plo once beat Yoda in a duel. "I've heard you're one of the only Jedi to have ever beaten Master Yoda in a duel." However, this is only a very brief mention. We know nothing of what exactly happened in the duel, whether or not Yoda was holding back, or any other relevant factors. It’s even possible it was a rumor. Still, the fact that Plo Koon is even remotely comparable to Yoda in even one source is a massive testament to his power and skill. It’s no coincidence that the only way the clones killed Plo was unexpectedly when he was stuck in his ship. Had they attacked him on the battlefield, it’s likely that Plo would’ve made it out alive. Combining Koon’s skill with Mace’s saber prowess, Sidious would’ve stood no chance.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who is the richest among all the DC and Marvel superheroes? Why?
Answer: That would be Thor, by far. Thor ruled the most powerful nation in the world — the same nation that kept treasures from various realms. Odin’s vault was prized all around the universe, and gold was as common on Asgard as water. The true extent of Thor’s wealth could be in the quadrillions of dollars.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why is Thanos so strong? Was he born that way?
Answer: Thanos was a mutant. In comics, we learn that Thanos’ mother was a Titan (Sui-San) and his father was an Eternal (A’lars). While his siblings were “normal”, the Mad Titan was a “defective” gene who was very different from everyone else. This led to the Purple Giant becoming an “outcast” in society, being looked down upon by his peers. It’s what eventually led to him becoming a ruthless warrior.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is DC doing wrong that Marvel is doing right?
Answer: One word: consistency. Therein lies the biggest issue with the DCEU. It’s hard to hype people up for a movie when its universe gets replaced every five years. Take, for example, Batman: Don’t get me wrong, most of the Batman actors we see on the big screen (my personal favorites being Keaton and Affleck) played their roles perfectly, but the fact remains that the level of attachment one may have to the character diminishes every time they’re recast. This is where Marvel really shines. The entire MCU is so perfectly consistent, each with characters of their own being introduced, but in a way that does not contradict each other. In fact, the writers make the MCU so well-knit that many viewers (including myself) often take pride in finding even a minor plot hole. But more importantly, the characters are very rarely recast. And if they are, they’re for such minor characters that most casual viewers don’t even notice a change. You could never imagine, for example, anyone else playing Iron Man except RDJ. And you’ll never imagine another Captain America other than Chris Evans. It’s this tight-knit, consistent, and decade-long culmination of numerous films coming together in such a harmonious fashion that makes the MCU so enticing to viewers. It’s what sets it apart from every other franchise, and it’s why the MCU has become far more legendary than DC could ever hope to be.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did Tyrion make a mistake by killing Tywin Lannister?
Answer: Absolutely. Tywin was a mastermind of war and tactics. He understood the political landscape better than anyone, and he routinely made clear how far behind his children were when it came to logistics. When it comes to keeping the sanctity of House Lannister intact, there was no one greater than the mighty Tywin. The moment Tywin died, all hell broke lose. Cersei foolishly used the High Sparrow for the short-term gain of “dealing with Margaery” without taking into account the long-term issues with giving a common man who the people loved absolute power. Then Tommen, the sweet but relatively dumb kid he was, bought into the lies of the High Sparrow and turned King’s Landing into a theocracy. Had Tywin been alive, he never would’ve allowed the High Sparrow to have the kind of power that was given to him. Tywin was too rational to do something so foolish. With Tywin alive, Margaery and Tommen would have continued on the throne alive and well, with his grandfather pulling the strings behind the scenes. There’s also another benefit with Tywin: The war. The only reason Cersei refused to aid the war effort against the White Walkers was because of her own pride and arrogance. Tywin was no fool—he’d know that the only way to protect his family was by protecting mankind. Thus, he’d aid Daenerys’ effort against the White Walkers. With this temporary “alliance”, it’s likely perhaps a truce could be put into effect with both the North and South. Tyrion was influential in many (not all) of Daenerys’ dealings, so perhaps he’d talk some sense into the Queen to not go on a full-scale war against the South. In the end, it would come to a point where Tywin’s hand would be forced—surrender or burn. Tywin was not foolish enough to fight a war he couldn’t win, his ultimate goal was to preserve the sanctity of his House. Had he been forced to surrender to Daenerys’ forces, he absolutely would’ve until he won the long game and hit back when the time was right. Tywin would never have dragged on the war against Daenerys like Cersei did. He’d have ended the conflict then and lived in harmony, either by a dirty trick or through a genuine surrender. It’s better than being dead.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What would be Tywin Lannister’s reaction if the walk of shame happened while he was alive?
Answer: It never would’ve happened in the first place. Remember what Tywin said about his family and legacy: “Do you know what legacy means? It’s what you pass down to your children and to your children’s children. It’s what remains of you when your gone.” “The House that puts his family first will always defeat the House that puts the whims and wishes of his sons and daughters first”. The legacy and sanctity of his House meant everything to Tywin. To him, it was the reason for his existence—to further the legacy of his House. Tywin honored and cherished the Lannister name, even when it didn’t suit him. Tyrion, perhaps Tywin’s most hated person, was still given the title of a prince and (briefly) the Lord’s Hand—all because Tywin didn’t let personal hatred influence the fact that Tyrion still held the Lannister name. The very idea of such an esteemed Lannister noblewoman being desecrated by the commoners of King’s Landing would be an unfathomable thought for Tywin. He would never have let it happen. The whole rise of power by the High Sparrow would’ve been thwarted long before, had Tywin been around. But if he was forced into the situation of Cersei about to be in a walk of atonement, Tywin would’ve bathed the streets of King’s Landing with blood before Cersei ever took a step.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Like Tyrion Lannister, you are convicted for a crime. You have the option of Trial by combat. The opposite knight is none other than Hulk. Which MCU character you would choose as your champion?
Answer: Well, it’s certainly not going to be easy. The Green Monster is no joke. He’s incalculably strong, lightning fast, and freakishly big. He could very easily slaughter many (if not, most) MCU heroes like Falcon, Ant-Man, Hawkeye, Black Widow, and Captain America—just to name a few. Hell, he could likely take on some A-listers like Mark 85 Iron Man, Spiderman, and base Thor. However, there are a number of individuals that I could choose who could wipe the floor with angry Banner. But just to play it safe, I’ll go overkill with Ego. The guy is literally an immortal planet and and celestial who lived for millions of years. His powerful was great enough to conquer the entire world if his son (who had his same powers) didn’t intervene. There are very few individuals I can name within the MCU that stand a chance against the reality-warping being, and Hulk certainly isn’t one of them.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if there was a white Black Panther?
Answer: In comics, there already is one. He’s referred to as the White Wolf (just like Bucky is in the MCU), but his real name is Hunter. When he was a child, Hunter and his family had crash-landed in Wakanda, so King T’Chaka decided to adopt and train him. Technically, Hunter is T’Challa’s brother. Hunter eventually became a warrior (like the Black Panther), completely loyal to Wakanda. The MCU likes to change up things from comics or cartoons, so it’s likely that Bucky is just their version of the White Wolf. And with this, it’s plausible that we’ll see this mantle of White Wolf used in the future for Bucky to serve the people of Wakanda in their time of need, for everything they’d done for him.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Thanos worthy of wielding Mjolnir?
Answer: Absolutely not. Notice Thanos’ grip on worthy Cap’s arm back in Endgame: The Mad Titan clearly shows difficulty even taking Cap’s arm, let alone trying to take Mjolnir. Even he knew he wasn’t worthy of the hammer, so instead of trying to take it (and fail), he uses Cap’s own hand and throws it away. Remember the enchantment Odin made: The only way one can become “worthy” to hold the hammer is either by: I don’t think Mjolnir would consider universal genocide as “worthy morals”.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Was Justin Hammer the best villain in the MCU?
Answer: Absolutely not. Don’t get me wrong, the guy is fun to watch and Sam Rockwell played him to perfection, but he’s just not that interesting. But that was his purpose—he wasn’t supposed to be interesting, he was just another throwaway villain. Hammer is a wannabe villain with no true intention other than financial profit. He uses other, smarter people’s ideas and takes credit for it himself, and tries to undermine those actually making a difference (sounds like a certain SpaceX owner). There are a solid number of far more intriguing MCU villains than Hammer. While some could be debated, I’ll name the obvious ones: Thanos, Loki, Zemo, Killmonger, Alexander Pierce, and Vulture. There are others that could be mentioned, but these are what I believe everyone can agree are far better-written than Hammer. And again, no hate to the actor or character, it’s just that he’s not made to be super intriguing.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What was the reason for Loki betraying Thor for Thanos, but not for Hela?
Answer: Hela had what he wanted—Thanos didn’t. Loki’s entire drive for betraying his father and brother was for one reason: to rule on a throne (Asgard in particular). Loki had believed that it was his birthright—he was owed it since his birth. He even had it for a few years, and he enjoyed it very much. Thanos never cared to have a throne, per se. He was totally fine with Loki ruling Earth, as long as he gave him the Infinity Stones on the planet. Loki was simply a step in Thanos’ ultimate purpose of “righteous genocide”. Hela, on the other hand, wanted the one thing Loki wanted—the Asgardian throne. And what’s more, she demanded he kneel to her. As egotistical Loki was, it took him aback: Loki’s glorious purpose was to rule as a king. He could do that under Thanos, but not under Hela.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Can one become a chess grandmaster starting at 38 years old?
Answer: Unfortunately, no. High level chess is an incredibly cognitive-intensive game. It uses the brain on a scale that many people could not realize it could perform. This ability to be able to see 3–5 moves in advance is something that needs to be adapted over time, and the only way to do this is by starting at a young age. Nearly every single grandmaster in chess history started learning at a very young age—almost all between the ages of 6–11. One famous anomaly of this was Chinese GM Ye Jiangchuan, who started at the age of 17. His case was remarkable and very uncommon, and yet Jiangchuan wasn’t even an adult when he started! Theoretically, yes—it’s not outside the realm of possibility that an adult could become a GM if they started at 38. But practically, it is near-impossible. The brain starts deteriorating at the age of 25, and unless you have a solid foundation of chess before that level, it is almost certain that you will never become a master of any sort in chess (let alone becoming a Grandmaster). In fact, it is for this reason (as well as the fact that chess makes pretty much no money, even as a Grandmaster) that many Grandmasters in their 30s and 40s retire from the game altogether. A famous example of this was GM James Tarjan.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Thor throw Mjolnir at Hela without even knowing her that much?
Answer: Remember what Odin told both Thor and Loki just moments before they met Hela: Odin: It’s already begun, she’s coming. My life was all that held her back, but my time has come. I cannot keep her away any longer. Thor: Father, what are you talking about? Odin: Goddess of Death. Hela, my firstborn—your sister. Thor: Your what? Odin: Her violent appetites grew beyond my control. I couldn’t stop her, so I imprisoned her. She draws her strength from Asgard. Once she gets there, her powers will be…limitless. Odin warned Thor of just how dangerous Hela truly was. He told his sons about just how violent she was, as well as how strong she became and how strong she will become. When the Allfather himself—a man revered across the universe as an unstoppable force—says that someone is too powerful for him to stop, you best believe she’s a threat that needs to be neutralized immediately. And that’s what Thor did (or, more accurately, tried to do).

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did Mjolnir originally belong to Hela?
Answer: In comics, no. The original wielder of Mjolnir was a younger version of Odin. The Allfather had used the weapon to assist him in solidifying Asgard into the level of prestige and power it later became. The MCU, however, might be different. We don’t know exactly how old Mjolnir truly is. We don’t know when it was made, but we do know it happened long before Thor ever came into the picture. Hela did use Mjolnir throughout her time conquering the nine realms with her father. However, this doesn’t mean Hela was the original wielder of Mjolnir. All we know was that at some point, it was forged through the heart of a dying star. This could’ve traced back to Odin’s era of being a young man, or even his father Bor’s time. The official MCU Wiki page claims that Odin wielded it before Hela, and passed it down to her. There isn’t enough evidence in canon to support this. Perhaps Odin’s father Bor made the weapon, or maybe Odin had it made for Hela specifically.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Was Hela worthy of Mjolnir?
Answer: Yes. All too often, people tend to completely misunderstand the enchantment Odin put onto Mjolnir. It isn’t about perfection in the slightest. Notice what it says: Whosoever holds this hammer, if he be worthy, shall possess the power of Thor.” So then the obvious question: What does it mean to be worthy? Well, worthiness doesn’t necessarily have to mean a “western” idea of morality/ethics. If that were the case, not even Thor (a guy ruling an imperialist nation that has stolen from thousands of planets) would be worthy to wield Mjolnir. Instead, what it means to be “worthy” is being worthy to rule Asgard—to be able to make Asgard prosper under the right principles of ruling. Hela fit this description perfectly. See, Hela was the firstborn—she was the rightful ruler of Asgard. She was also a firm warrior who brought Asgard to its peak in the past. There is no reason to believe that she would not be any more unworthy to wield Mjolnir than Thor. This could also explain why she managed to hold and break the hammer with relative ease.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who would win between Surtur vs Thanos?
Answer: Without the stones, Thanos stands absolutely no chance. Surtur at the peak of his power was a near-unstoppable force—only Odin in his prime (a guy who, in comics, beat both Thanos and Silver Surfer combined) was able to defeat him. Surtur managed to incinerate the most powerful world in the nine realms in a matter of minutes. Hela, the goddess of death, has shown powers to be near-equal to Thanos. And yet she never stood a damn chance against the fiery beast. However, Thanos with the stones is a different story. Thanos has a lot of options to destroy Surtur with the Infinity Stones. He could use the space stone to teleport him to Boston, he could use the soul stone to suck the life out of him, or he could use the reality stone to turn him into spaghetti. The stones would make Thanos the most powerful being in the universe.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Could Omni-Man destroy the Justice League?
Answer: Heh, not a chance. Nolan (and the rest of the Viltrumites, for that matter) are criminally overrated in comparison with Marvel and DC characters. Their feats are simply far below the likes of some of the most famous heroes we know and love—Viltrumites are planetary level threats at best, while some Marvel/DC characters can be multiversal level threats. Let’s go through the roster: At best, Nolan could take on 2–3 of the weakest Justice League members. The others are just far above his paygrade.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is the summary of Thor Ragnarok?
Answer: Fire Guy says he wants to destroy Point Break’s floating island of a nation. So, Point Break kills him. Point Break goes back to floaty nation with Fire Guy’s head, only to see that Trickster Guy is living up to his name. So, Point Break makes Trickster Guy show him where Dad is. Trickster Guy can’t find Dad. So, Bleecker Street Magician helps them find him. Point Break and Trickster Guy talk with Dad. Dad tells them of their unknown Mean Sister and yeets. Point Break and Trickster Guy try to kill Mean Sister. They fail. Point Break gets captured by Drunk Lady. Drunk Lady takes Point Break to Jeff Goldblum. Jeff Goldblum makes Point Break fight Green Man. Meanwhile, Mean Sister is being mean to everyone on the floating island. Point Break recruits Drunk Lady and Green Man to his side. Point Break then breaks out of Jeff Goldblum's world. Point Break fights Mean Sister, then loses an eye. Point Break then gains the power of friendship and kills zombies. Trickster Guy comes to floaty island with an escape ship. Point Break tells Trickster Guy to unleash Fire Guy. Fire Guy is unleashed and kills Mean Sister. The good guys escape. Everyone watches as their beloved island is destroyed. But everyone is happy about being saved. Then a Mean Purple guy ruins everything.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why couldn’t Emperor Palpatine defend himself from Darth Vader when he threw him down the shaft?
Answer: Well, he did—but it wasn’t enough. In the last few seconds of his life, Palpatine was able to fry the Chosen One so badly that it led him to him being on the verge of death. I’d definitely call that “defending himself”. So, why didn’t Sidious do more before Anakin killed him? Because of his overconfidence. Remember what Luke told the Emperor: Notice how the Sith Lord doesn’t even correct him—he’s well aware of his weakness being overconfidence! At that point, Sidious was consumed with the indulgence of money, fame, and power. He became engrossed in the inaccurate assumption that he was now an invincible god whose will always comes to fruition. And what was Sidious’ will now? To turn Luke—or kill him. Either worked for the Sith Lord, and at that moment he enjoyed the fact that not only could he control the Chosen One, but also his son as well. Palpatine didn’t sense Vader’s turn because he had no reason to think he would. Vader had been his loyal lapdog for decades now, doing unfathomable things for the Empire. By all logic, Anakin was dead and buried years ago. But what neither Palpatine (or even Vader, for that matter) realized was that Anakin was still inside the cold Sith heart—and through the love for his son, that passion and will reignited to do what Anakin was always destined to do—destroy the Sith.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is something that you noticed in Thor Ragnarok?
Answer: We were told of Frigga’s powers ahead of time. Remember what Loki says to Thor toward the beginning of Thor: Ragnarok: Loki is implying here that witches can, indeed, see the future. This ability to see through time is exactly what Frigga (a woman raised by witches) managed to do in Endgame:

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are some examples of bad sportsmanship you have witnessed in chess?
Answer: Anything involving Hikaru Nakamura. I’m surprised how overlooked it is that Hikaru (especially when he was in his 20s) was notorious for his inability to take losses well. And unlike folks like Magnus, Hikaru doesn’t just get mad at himself during losses—he takes it out on others. One great example of this was in the 2015 Gibraltar Chess Tournament, when he cussed out GM David Howell when he made a draw in a losing position: “I once drew with [Hikaru] in Gibraltar when he was six out of six and I was half a point back. I was very lucky, I was probably losing the whole game and I managed to hold it, and then afterward he was really rude to me. He said that I was ‘so f’ing lucky’ and that I ‘had no f’ing understanding’, and then he stormed off…And then his dad came to apologize on his behalf, but I never heard an apology from him.” Hikaru also has had a number of toxic streaming moments. One famous example was when he insulted GM Daniel Naroditsky after losing to him because of a dirty trick (something Nakamura himself has done to others plenty): “Ridiculous. The guy plays garbage and loses every game, then wins two games he has no business winning.” Hypocrisy at its finest. There was also that time Hikaru lost to GM Luis Supi, the #1 Brazilian chess player. Because of his loss, he accused Supi of cheating. “The time usage here is really disturbing me. This feels like a 99% game.” *Hikaru goes to check the accuracy, and is proven wrong* “I guess this is reasonable…nothing too crazy, but the 30 second usage on multiple moves is suspicious.”

Name: Crantzer
Question: Where is Yoda in The Acolyte?
Answer: Well, Yoda is definetly alive when The Acolyte takes place. Yoda was around 800 years old at the time of The Phantom Menace and became a Jedi Knight on Coruscant by the age of 100. The show, meanwhile, takes place only 100 years before The Phantom Menace. Thus, it is clear that Yoda was not only alive during the time of this High Republic era, but he was also likely a high-ranking member of the Order (if not already the Grandmaster). So, will the green Jedi make an appearance? It’s likely. The entire investigation that Master Sol is conducting is very top secret, even within the Order. Only certain top, high-ranking Jedi are even aware of it—I’d reckon Yoda is high on that list by this time. So, perhaps he will make a minor appearance in the show, perhaps even toward the end. Of course, it is also possible that the show wants to keep a level of originality and only introduce new characters, so we may not get Yoda after all. But based on the progression of the show so far, I’d bet that he (or some other old Jedi like Plo Koon) will make at least some sort of appearance.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Which Jedi would have survived Order 66 if they weren’t taken by surprise?
Answer: That would be, by far, Plo Koon. It’s no coincidence that Plo was killed off in a surprise attack inside his ship rather than in close combat. The guy was a legend within the Order, easily being among the top 5 most powerful at the time. He was no joke. During the Battle of Khorm, Koon was able to overpower Asajj Ventress—someone who had been trained by Dooku himself and who went toe-to-toe with both Anakin and Obi-Wan on numerous occasions. Plo was also the second greatest pilot in the Galaxy. He was undefeated in terms of pilot fighting skill. In the game The Clone Wars: Lightsaber Duels, it is also mentioned by Anakin Skywalker that Koon once beat Yoda himself in a duel. "I've heard you're one of the only Jedi to have ever beaten Master Yoda in a duel." However, as it’s only a brief mention, we know nothing of what exactly happened in the duel, whether or not Yoda was holding back, or any other relevant factors. It’s even possible it was a rumor. Still, the fact that Plo Koon is even remotely comparable to Yoda in even one source is a massive testament to his power and skill. If anyone should’ve survived Order 66, it was Plo. He is probably the most underrated, powerful, and kind-hearted Jedi that we know of in canon. In fact, it’s not out of the question that Plo survived. All we saw was his ship explode—perhaps he managed to escape (I certainly wouldn’t put it past him). There’s even a very intriguing and enjoyable fanfiction about this very situation, written by the legendary writer Cade Oosthuizen.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if Anakin was Mace Windu's Padawan?
Answer: Things would turn out a lot better for both Anakin and the rest of the Order. Sure, Obi-Wan was a good guy and a powerful Jedi—but he was young and inexperienced. He had a very hard time all throughout their relationship to train and discipline the Chosen One himself, a guy who also happened to be emotionally unstable on occasion. What Anakin needed was a father figure in his life, not a brother like Kenobi. While someone like Yoda or Plo Koon could fill that role of father figure nicely, (despite what some may think) Mace Windu would have been the best master for Anakin. Unlike other Jedi masters, Mace knew what it was like to feel the dark side call to him. And unlike everyone else, he didn’t forbid the dark side—instead, he mastered control over it. Anakin was very much in a similar state. He often had aspects of the dark side slowly creep into him, which made him more and more unstable. A master like Windu would have been tremendously helpful to learn to not suppress the dark side (like Obi-Wan taught), but to have control over it.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is the Stark Malibu mansion real? How and where did they shoot the films?
Answer: No, it’s not real—but the location is. Stark’s mansion is shown to be located just off of Point Dume, a promontory on the coast of Malibu. This is what it looks like in the movies: This is the real location where it was taken: The house was completely CGI, and it was edited into the film in post-production. But the view, nonetheless, is as gorgeous in the movies as it is in real life.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did the Emperor not see Vader turning on him in Return of the Jedi?
Answer: No. Remember what Luke told the Emperor just moments before Vader’s betrayal: Notice how the Sith Lord doesn’t even correct him—he’s well aware of his weakness being overconfidence! Ever since he was a young apprentice under Plagueis, Sidious was always a cautious man. But all of that changed the moment he got what he had always wanted—unlimited power. At that point, Sidious was consumed with the indulgence of money, fame, and power. He became engrossed in the inaccurate assumption that he was now an invincible god whose will always comes to fruition. And what was Sidious’ will now? To turn Luke—or kill him. Either worked for the Sith Lord, and at that moment he enjoyed the fact that not only could he control the Chosen One, but also his son as well. Palpatine didn’t sense Vader’s turn because he had no reason to think he would. Vader had been his loyal lapdog for decades now, doing unfathomable things for the Empire. By all logic, Anakin was dead and buried years ago. But what neither Palpatine (or even Vader, for that matter) realized was that Anakin was still inside the cold Sith heart—and through the love for his son, that passion and will reignited to do what Anakin was always destined to do—destroy the Sith. In that moment, Anakin killed two of the greatest Sith Lords to ever exist.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who's faster: Quicksilver or the Flash?
Answer: Whether it be comics or movie versions, the Flash is exponentially faster. This is the same Flash who literally beat death by running to the edge of the universe, altered time through phazing, saved an entire city in under a microsecond, and ran on clouds. The guy is seriously OP. Quicksilver is definitely fast, but he is no match for the Flash in any universe. The reason is mainly because of how utilized and cracked the Flash is written to be (as opposed to Quicksilver being a much less-used character). Hell, even in the MCU, Pietro wasn’t fast enough not to get shot by dozens of bullets!

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are the most unknown things in Marvel comics?
Answer: Thanos is a master troller. In the Thanos Annual Vol 2 comics, we see Thanos purposefully and menacingly troll an innocent guy every birthday he’s had. On his birthday, the Mad Titan would show up and give a more-than-inconvenient gift. All the while, no one believes the poor guy.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How does Magnus Carlsen handle defeats?
Answer: Very, very poorly. Even Magnus admits he is the most sore loser of chess. Because of the pressure he has as both the world #1 and (arguably) GOAT of the game, Magnus always expects to win. So when he doesn’t, it is usually an unexpected disappointment. A very good example was the 2016 World Blitz Championship, where—despite being in second place—Magnus was so disappointed that he stormed off stage. Another example was at the 2021 Meltwater Champions Chess Tour, where Magnus blundered a Back-Rank Mate against Wesley So. That being said, Magnus always has sportsmanship. Unlike a lot of people (in a lot of sports), Magnus doesn’t take his frustration or anger out on the the opponent who beat him. He blames only himself. Carlsen puts himself on such a high standard that he becomes angry when he doesn’t meet his own standards. Because of this, Magnus always remains respectful to his opponents, even when he’s angry at himself.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How strong is the strongest version of Captain America?
Answer: In comics, that would be Soldier Supreme. This version of Steve was injected with a super soldier serum that was infused with magical properties. It allowed for him to perfect both physical strength and mastery of the mystic arts. Some of this version of Cap’s best feats were that he managed to Spirit Walk on occasion (something we’ve only seen Wanda do in the MCU), and he even beat a version of Dormammu called Dormammu Red. In the MCU, it would be Worthy Captain America. While we don’t see a lot of progress for Cap in terms of power throughout the MCU, his worthy version (when he wielded Mjolnir) was his most powerful. With it, he possessed the powers of Thor—including superhuman strength and durability. It’s how he managed to give the Mad Titan a run for his money (at least for a couple minutes).

Name: Crantzer
Question: If you could add a single line to Avengers: Endgame, what would it be?
Answer: While there are some good answers here, there is another line that I think takes the cake. Thanos had his own vision scene—Tony didn’t. Well, he did but the directors decided to cut it from the movie. The deleted scene was that of him and an older version of his daughter Morgan. While this was a nice, sentimental, and final impact for him, I do think something better would be that he had met Yinsen instead. Remember Yinsen’s last words to Tony before he died: Tony took that lesson to heart, no doubt. I feel like a much more impactful, one-lined scene would’ve been something like this: Tony enters the afterlife. In shock, he notices the face of an old friend. Surely, this is a hallucination. Yinsen then looks at him and simply says one thing:

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is Palpatine's motivation for wanting Luke in The Empire Strikes Back (Star Wars movie)?
Answer: Well, one reason is that Palpatine needed a replacement. While he was still by far the second most powerful Force user in the Galaxy, Vader was getting old. Palpatine knew that, at some point, he would have to find a new apprentice. Who better to find than the Chosen One’s son? At the point that Palpatine found and met Luke, the young Skywalker was at the perfect age for manipulating—he was strong in the Force, yet he wasn’t completely matured into the light side (or so Sidious thought), and he also wasn’t skilled enough to beat him. Luke was new to the whole Jedi thing, after all. What better time to brainwash him than now? In the end, Palpatine’s ultimate goal was to continue ruling the Empire with an iron fist, a Skywalker being his enforcer. He was also in the process of working on eternal life through cloning, so Vader would not last as long as he would. It all comes down to timing. Palpatine was as close to manipulating Luke as he’d ever get, and he’d have been a valuable asset to the Empire—even more valuable than he was for the Rebels.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Firouzja as good as Carlsen at his age?
Answer: Not really. Firouzja is currently 20 years old. While he is undoubtedly exceptional for his age, Magnus was a different breed. When Magnus was the same age (back in 2012), he had already solidified himself as the #1 chess player in the world. Firouzja, on the other hand, currently stands at 15th in the world. Of course, rating does not necessarily equate skill. But in terms of exceptionality and how legendary they are at the same age, Magnus takes the cake. It’s hard to outclass the (arguably) greatest player of all time, no matter age.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Which team are you on: Team Cap or Team Iron Man? Why?
Answer: Neither. The one person who got it right the entire time was Natasha. See, Nat understood that being in accordance with the law while also operating as a hero was the safest option. She wasn’t immediately hostile toward the government from the get-go, and she tried to come up with a realistic solution by mixing both heroic efforts and accountability. But the problem arose when things started getting out of hand. Nat started realizing that this tension was more than just political differences—Cap was just trying to protect his friend. And the icing on the cake for her was likely upon finding out that not only was Wanda locked in her room, but Clint went out of retirement to help her. It was at that point that Nat knew the Accords had gone too far. Nat understood that, at that point, she was on the wrong side. And once she understood that, she had the courage to act on it. That’s what it means to pick right: When you go with your gut, even when everyone and everything else tells you the opposite.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Jesus a freak?
Answer: Oh, yes. Jesus is the very definition of breaking down societal norms. From His life on Earth to His death and resurrection, nothing Jesus does is something we consider “normal”. Absolutely none of these things would be something we as humans can do rationally. Our very nature is completely contrary to being able to submit to others or choosing others over ourselves. Jesus was completely unusual for both His time and ours, and anyone who puts their trust in Him and believes in His name will also be called a freak. It’s because this way of living is so foreign to the rest of the world.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who would win, Thanos with the Infinity Gauntlet (comics) or the Star Wars universe?
Answer: The Mad Titan would eviscerate the entire Star Wars Universe. You have to understand, even Thanos without the stones was already incredibly powerful in his own universe. He has soloed every Avenger on numerous occasions, overpowered Thor (who had the power stone), and even fought on par with the planet-eating Galactus! The Marvel Universe is also a lot more vast than Star Wars, seeing as it has a numerous galaxies, whereas Star Wars is restricted to just one. With the stones, Thanos would basically be a god. Thanos would be able to control reality, time, and space (just to name a few). These very things were powers that Sidious (arguably the most powerful Force user) could only ever dream of achieving. Even the gods of the Star Wars universe (like the Mortis) have power constraints. Given the ability to control all matter in the universe, it’s more than likely that Thanos could get rid of them as well. In the end, if Thanos wanted to, he could be the last remaining living being in the Star Wars universe.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Can you name some of the most powerful Jedi in Star Wars who are not main characters?
Answer: The most powerful non-crucial character isn’t who you think. It’s this guy: That is Cin Drallig. Drallig is a notoriously underrated Jedi—he taught the finest of warriors including Obi-Wan and Anakin. Cin had a reputation among the Jedi as being the second greatest duelist in the Jedi Order, second only to Yoda himself (however, I’d argue that Mace took the place of second). Because of his legendary skill and wisdom, Drallig was also the Chief of Security at the Jedi Temple. Though it is brief, we do see Vader manage to kill the Jedi master in hologram footage: However, the RoTS game adaption gives the guy much more justice:

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who is the fastest between Bucky, Captain America and Black Panther? (MCU)
Answer: Notice Cap and T’Challa’s run in Infinity War: It seems like although T’Challa had around a couple seconds of a head start, Steve made it to the destination almost immediately after him. It makes it seem like, perhaps, Cap is slightly faster than the Black Panther. This is, of course, is not the only time we’ve seen both Cap and T’Challa run. We know for a fact that Steve, T’Challa, and Bucky are around the same speed based on their foot pursuit: However, the cars were major obstacles in this scene. It’s only in Infinity War that we managed to see who might be a slightly faster runner—Steve. The difference in speed between all three enhanced individuals are very minor, if any. But from what I’ve seen, it seems to me that Cap (and consequentially, Bucky as well) is just a touch faster than T’Challa in terms of speed.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Magnus Carlsen close to losing the no.1 spot?
Answer: Absolutely. Magnus is already dangerously close to losing his #1 mark. Legends like Levon Aronian and Hikaru Nakamura have beat him on occasion—so much so that it isn’t necessarily a shock to see. While Magnus still may win a small majority of the time, he must still be very careful against such players. There have also been some very impressive new players who have shown their skill to be extraordinarily phenomenal. Perhaps the most famous rising young star is the 18-year old Praggnanandhaa Rameshbabu, who (while still beneath Magnus in terms of skill) has beat the world #1 on numerous occasions. There’s also the teenage prodigy and current contender for the World Championship, 18-year old Dommaraju Gukesh. He has managed to beat some top players in the past few years, including Magnus at the 2023 Norway Blitz Tournament. With this new wave of brilliant young minds within the chess community, we will see such players boost in skill and prowess over the board. All the while, Magnus will likely not be as participant or dominant in chess as he used to be. It is thus more than likely that in the next coming years (perhaps within the next decade), Magnus will lose his #1 spot in the world.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why do some experts consider Bobby Fischer the greatest chess player ever?
Answer: It’s not for the reasons you think. Some of the current top players (like Magnus and Hikaru) could likely beat Fischer in a 1v1—and yet, the argument can still be made that Bobby Fischer was the greatest player of all time for one reason: his accuracy. See, folks like Magnus and Hikaru were born in the day and age of the computer. Unlike Bobby’s time of high-level guesswork, a computer can now tell you what the objectively best move is. Unlike before, the best move would simply be a common consensus. But today, even the greatest chess minds doubt their moves, because they know the computer can always find what they can’t. With this day of superhuman-advanced chess analysis, there also came a number of new theories and openings. Fischer was more impressive. Despite being without hundreds of theories and tactics that currently exist today, Fischer has routinely proved himself to be capable of making top engine moves in some of his games. For example, he managed to beat the legendary Donald Bryne with an accuracy of 97%! Fischer was truly ahead of his time. Fischer’s average accuracy in his life is at a staggering 92.52%. This is just 0.71% short of the current greatest player, in an era where the amount of Stockfish preparation is what decides a win or loss. There’s no telling what a mind like Fischer’s would have been able to accomplish with today’s new understanding of chess. But we know for certain that he still holds a chance against some of the greatest minds even today. Fischer can and always will be a legend in the chess world, and in my mind he is the greatest player of all time.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who are the most intelligent chess players?
Answer: While it is true that folks like Magnus, Anand and Nakamura are quite intelligent, there is one who is often overlooked: Ding Liren. You see, unlike every other top chess player, Ding is also an academic. Liren got his Law Degree from Peking University, which is one of the most prestigious schools in China and boasts an undergraduate admission rate of just 1%. While immigration is a big part as to why he has not participated in a number of tournaments, the reason for Ding’s 8-month absence following his World Championship win was partly due to the fact that he has a full-time job as a lawyer. Ding is not just one of the strongest chess players in the world today—he’s also an incredibly gifted and studious individual. The fact that Ding is a full-time, decorated lawyer on one hand and the Chess World Champion on the other (while no other top player has a separate job) goes to show just how impressive he truly is. He is tremendously underrated.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How good are the Botez sisters, Alexandra and Andrea, at chess?
Answer: Pretty damn good. Alexandra is a WFM with a FIDE rating of 2011, which is already much more than most. She’s also in the 96.94th percentile of registered chess players in the US, which makes her within the top 3.06% of players. And mind you, this doesn’t include casual, nonregistered chess players (which would make her in the 99.99th percentile). Andrea is also quite good. While she is not a master, Andrea does having a FIDE rating of 1906 (which isn’t that far behind her sister). That already makes her in the top 5.38% of registered US chess players. The only reason some consider Alex and Andrea relatively weak is because they both often deal with players far above their paygrade. Guys like Hikaru and Magnus manage to beat both sisters so quickly and decisively that it almost feels like they’re beginners. However, what you have to understand is that both of these guys are anything but your average player—they’re among some of the top chess players in human history. Are the Botez sisters good? Absolutely. But are they among the top players? Absolutely not.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Could Alexandra Botez become a grandmaster someday?
Answer: Absolutely not. Don’t get me wrong, Alex is definitely an impressive player in the grand scheme of things. She’s a WFM with a FIDE rating of 2011, which is already much more than most. She’s also in the 96.94th percentile of registered chess players in the US, which makes her within the top 3.06% of players. And mind you, this doesn’t include casual, nonregistered chess players (which would make her in the 99.99th percentile). That being said, the title of GM is something else entirely. Getting the title of GM means you must having a rating of at least 2500, and you must have favorable results in at least 27 tournaments with Grandmasters present. Alex has been floating the rating of 2000 for many years. At this rate, it seems like her peak. On top of this, she’s not too active in tournaments involving higher level players (for obvious reasons). Levy Rozman—an IM for far too long—hasn’t even achieved the title of GM, and he crushes both Botez sisters frequently. Sadly, it’s next to impossible for Alexandra to ever become a GM.

Name: Crantzer
Question: *SPOILER* How come Dr. Strange can defeat Dormammu but not Thanos?
Answer: I’d hardly call any of these a win for Strange: Dormammu was far more powerful than Strange could ever even fathom. There was no way he’d be able to defeat him by power alone. Strange died many times by Dormammu’s hand. Strange only managed to save the universe by using the time stone to create an infinite loop, and he’d only free Dormammu from the loop if he left his world alone. Essentially, Strange bored Dormammu to submission.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Will we ever have someone greater than Magnus Carlsen?
Answer: Never say never. In the 60s, no one thought anyone would be greater than Mikhal Tal. In the 70s, no one thought anyone would be greater than Bobby Fischer. In the 80s, no one thought anyone would be greater than Garry Kasparov. Notice a pattern here? Magnus is, by most accounts, the current GOAT of chess. But as time progresses, so can skill (especially with the development of new openings/theories and engines).
