While he is the greatest for now, there is no reason to think that Magnus will never be surpassed. In fact, there are a number of young, record-breaking, brilliant minds that do have a chance to surpass the Norwegian Grandmaster in due time.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why doesn't Dr Strange put Thanos in the Mirror Dimension without a slingring?
Answer: Well he tried, but it didn’t end well. Look back at this scene from Infinity War: Thanos used the OP power of the stones to absolutely wreck the mirror dimension while also turning it into an entire black hole to be sent back to the Sorcerer Supreme. And, to give credit where credit is due, Strange blocked it like a champ.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Was The Ancient One aware of Doctor Strange's existence before they met?
Answer: Oh, yes. The Ancient One knew everything about who Strange was and what he’d become years before he got into sorcery. She explains as much to Bruce Banner in 2012: The Ancient One knew everything that ever would or could happen up until her death. This was done by using the Time Stone.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Snyder use Steppenwolf (a non popular villain) in Justice League as a main villain?
Answer: It was a build up for a bigger villain. Steppenwolf wasn’t supposed to be the big bad guy for Snyder’s Justice League. The entire movie was supposed to be a buildup for Darkside’s conquest of Earth. The whole point was that Steppenwolf was a mild threat to the Justice League, so fact that Darkseid is revered as someone far above him in power brings fear and intrigue into seeing his character in the future. This is the same reason Whedon decided to use Loki in The Avengers. Loki managed to cause a very hard time for both SHIELD and the Avengers. He even managed to decimate a large part of New York with his power. And yet, this was nothing compared to the power of Thanos. It went to show just how formidable the Mad Titan was, without ever having to show him do anything.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Was Captain America about to fight Thanos’ entire army, by himself, before Strange brought everyone over?
Answer: Absolutely. Look again at how Cap single-handedly faced Thanos’ army: There was absolutely no hesitation with Steve — he was ready for a fight. Even when everyone else was down, he wasn’t. This isn’t anything new for Cap. He’s taken on people out of his paygrade all the time. Whether it be: Bullies twice his size, a HYDRA prison, a government agency, the entire world (and a friend), or the Mad Titan himself, Cap has always and will always continue to be a man who fights when no one else will. It’s just who he is. Steve stands up for what is right, even when he’s the last man standing.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are some things that just make no sense in the Star Wars movies?
Answer: Imperial ship designs. The Empire has had some criminally ineffective and hazardous workplaces for their workers. I mean, just look at their Star Destroyer command center: Definitely not meeting OSHA regulations. Where the hell are the safety railings on these things? One misstep on that squeaky-clean floor and someone could get seriously injured! The same goes for firing room in the Death Star: It seems cool and all, and I know that it wasn’t necessarily made for visitors — but one slip & fall, and you fry another valued member of the Empire. I’m not sure if this is just the Empire’s way of establishing survival of the fittest, but I don’t think it would hurt much to have some safety installments aboard the numerous ships/buildings that millions of Imperial workers pass through every day. But I suppose, being as corrupt and anti-welfare of a system as the Empire was, they cared more about economic profit than workers’ well-being.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did The Force want Order 66 to happen?
Answer: Yes. The Force willed Order 66 to happen not because it wanted less Jedi, but in order to accomplish the goal it set Anakin out to to in the first place. Remember, the prophecy was that Anakin would bring balance to the Force. The Jedi Order simply interpreted the prophecy to mean the eradication of the Sith. While this was true, what they didn’t understand was that it meant the eradication of their version of the Jedi, too. You see, at the time Order 66 was enacted, the Jedi Order was at its peak. They became a powerhouse within the Republic, and this heavy entailment into politics also resulted in the Order turning a blind eye to rampant corruption and even protecting those engaged in it. Dooku puts it well when he talks about Yoda: “The Jedi Order’s problem is Yoda. No being can wield that kind of power for centuries without becoming complacent at best or corrupt at worst. He has no idea that it’s overtaken him; he no longer sees all the little cumulative evils that the Republic tolerates and fosters, from slavery to endless wars, and he never asks, ‘Why are we not acting to stop this?’ Live alongside corruption for too long, and you no longer notice the stench.” I hate to agree with him, but it’s true. The Jedi needed a clean slate. Anakin completed what he was prophesied to do. The Chosen One brought balance to the Force. He did this by both destroying the (previous) Jedi, and the Sith. And after doing so, he allowed for his son to rebuild the Jedi into a more Force-centered and less corrupted version of the Order.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How did Tony Stark acquire nano-tech?
Answer: He made it. Tony had been tinkering with more accessible versions of Iron Man suits. The earliest design was the Mark 42, a suit he made fly to him and connect with him. It was through this inspiration of multi-connecting suit parts that Tony developed nanotech. Tony’s earliest development of nanotech was only years later with the Mark 46. It was in this suit that Tony allowed the suit to be summoned from anywhere with nanoparticles. This prototype were bulker in its earliest designs, but they eventually smoothened/thinned out into the nanoparticles we see in the Mark 50 and 85.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Heimdall send Hulk back to Earth and not Thor?
Answer: While there are some great answers here, there’s another aspect to this that people seem to forget. Remember what Thor said about the afterlife: Apparently, Asgardians can only get into Valhalla (a version of heaven) by dying in battle. It is a place of great prosperity, so it was a prized honor to die in battle. This is likely what led to Heimdall’s decision to send Bruce instead of Thor — everyone else on the ship besides Hulk would have went to Valhalla if they died (Thor included), because they died in battle. It was Heimdall’s way of sealing Thor an honorable fate, and saving Bruce’s.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Which superhero did Thanos fear the most?
Answer: Well, there is one that person that Thanos feared so much that he waited centuries until their death to get the stones: Odin. The All-Father was renowned across the universe as the most powerful being. He and the rest of Asgard were feared for their great strength. It’s why, despite the great treasures housed on Asgard, hardly anyone ever dared to attack — Thanos included. It’s no coincidence that the Mad Titan decided to strike just days after Odin’s passing. Thanos didn’t fear many people, but Odin sure as hell was one of them.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Should Disney replace Mark Hamill with Sebastian Stan as Luke Skywalker? Why or why not?
Answer: Absolutely. First off, the resemblance is uncanny. You won’t find anyone that looks more like a young Mark Hamill. Of course, another reason is because of VFX. The only alternative to having an actor like Stan play Luke is de-aging or completely deep faking a young Mark Hamill into every scene. While this is certainly possible (as shown in Book of Boba Fett), it’s never perfect and it just doesn’t feel as natural. Having a talented actor like Sebastian to look very closely (if not, more so than the VFX counterpart) to a young Hamill will make the appearance have all the more depth.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Will there ever be a female version of Captain America?
Answer: Well, we’ve already seen Peggy as Captain Carter in both What If and Multiverse of Madness. However, this might be the only female Captain America we’ll see in the MCU (at least for a few years). The mantle of Captain America was clearly given to Sam Wilson in Falcon and the Winter Soldier. Because of this, it’s unlikely anyone else will be taking the reigns soon (unless, of course, there is one shown from the multiverse.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Bruce Wayne a Catholic?
Answer: No. Bruce Wayne is by far the most skeptical, pessimistic man on the planet — he is the last person to believe in God. He’s as atheist as it comes. However, this was not always the case. In fact, as a kid, Bruce was quite religious. It was his life trauma that led him to distance himself from the idea of God.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is something you noticed in “Captain America: Civil War” that you believe others missed?
Answer: Cap knew Peter could lift the jetway before dropping it on him. I’ve seen some people asking an interesting question…why would Cap make such a move so as to drop a multi-ton jetway on a kid he just met? Literally any other human would’ve died from that! Surely, Cap wouldn’t try to kill Peter! If you thought the same, you’d be right — Cap wasn’t trying to kill Peter. He already knew he could hold it. How did he know this? Well, just moments before, Cap had an opportunity to test Peter’s strength: Peter managed to hold back a man with superhuman strength, so Steve knew that the jetway would have been no problem for him. Also, seeing as everyone was connected via some bluetooth device, it’s not out of the question to assume that Cap saw/heard about Peter nonchalantly grabbing Bucky’s arm.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Tony's gauntlet seem to hurt Hulk and Thanos the moment they wear the gauntlet. They even had difficulty performing the snap, but Tony didn't experience any difficulty wielding the gauntlet and snapping?
Answer: It may not be what you think. While it is true that Hulk and Thanos actively tried to stay alive after snapping while Tony didn’t, there is another reason to why Tony seemingly didn’t have as much difficulty: His armor. Look back at Tony’s snap: Notice how the energy is cutting through Tony’s armor (and later made it severely damaged)? It’s because the suit is absorbing enough of the Gauntlet’s energy to allow Tony to temporarily survive long enough to make the snap. It’s already established that it’s impossible for mortals to wield one Infinity Stone, let alone all six. [Peter holds Power Stone] Ronan: “You’re mortals…how?!” The very fact that Tony didn’t immediately get fried means he had help. And that help was his armor. People often underestimate Tony’s nanotech durability. It is immensely durable, and has handled some of the most powerful beings in the universe. Hell, it even took the force of the power stone on numerous occasions! While the suit didn’t stop Tony from dying (and certainly didn’t stop him from feeling pain), it did absorb the lion’s share of the energy so that he would not immediately die.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did Thanos save himself from being dusted or was he randomly spared in the Snap?
Answer: No. Take a look at Thanos’ reaction after the snap: Thanos has sort of a surprised look on his face that he still exists. This was because Thanos didn’t actually exclude himself from the snap. The Russo Brothers confirmed this was the case in an interview. Interviewer: What’s the possibility of Thanos killing himself when he snaps? Russo: The possibility of him doing it? Interviewer: Yeah. Russo: As a part of his random execution? He could’ve, and you can ask if he allowed himself to be a part of that random process…he does have a very interesting look on his face. When we come back to him after the snap, before he disappears, a look of surprise. Remember what Thanos said to strange: The Mad Titan’s entire philosophy was that his genocide was fair and balanced. It didn’t matter who you were — you weren’t exempt. Thanos was consumed with this philosophy, so the hypocrisy of exempting himself seems unlikely.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is the dumbest thing an MCU superhero did?
Answer: When Cap decided to crash the plane into the ice. It’s not like the plane was on autopilot. Steve clearly had control of the plane, so he could’ve easily just turned it around. The bombs also weren’t set to explode on a timer. Plus, Cap even got rid of most of them already. Another honorable mention is when Cap tried to choke out Ultron.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Can Magnus Carlsen beat an average (non-stupid) chess player if he gives a queen advantage?
Answer: Of course. The standard rule of thumb is that a queen trade is -1100 elo, according to chess.com. This means that to play fairly with Queen odds, the opponent should have a elo of around 1100 more than you. Magnus’ current elo stands at 2830, so he should be able to play with queen odds against someone rated 1730 or lower. Seeing as the global average chess player is around 800 elo, Magnus would absolutely crush them any day. Hell, I’m barely a novice and I could take an 800–900 without a Queen.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Will Magnus Carlsen surpass a 2900 rating?
Answer: Absolutely not. Magnus is at his life’s peak. He currently stands at a 2830 elo (which is historically outstanding), and he is already semi-retired from chess. You also have to understand that the greater the elo means the greater the loss against opponents. For example, Magnus once dominated and won a 2023 CCT Final, but in the process of doing so lost 9.6 elo points because of two losses against players much lower elo points than him. For Magnus, the increase in elo for every win against a 2600-2700 gives him drastically less elo than the loss of elo whenever he loses to such players. He’d have to pretty much always win against some of the top chess players — and even if he could, his participation in chess events has drastically decreased. What Magnus would need to do to even hope to reach 2900 is become much more active than he currently is, and he must have an almost unanimous win ratio because every loss is far worse than every win. This just isn’t realistic for the Norweigan Grandmaster, nor is it necessary — Magnus has nothing else to prove, he is already the greatest chess player in history. Reaching 2900 won’t change anything.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Thor richer than Black Panther?
Answer: Absolutely. While T’Challa is the wealthiest man on Earth, Thor’s homeworld was a power hub that used to keep the entire nine realms under heel. Thor ruled the most powerful nation in the world — the same nation that kept treasures from many different planets. Odin’s vault was prized all around the universe, and gold was as common in Asgard as water. So yes, Thor is exponentially richer than T’Challa.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who's stronger: Captain America or Black Panther?
Answer: In terms of pure strength (like in an arm wrestle), Cap would probably win. We’ve seen Rogers do some pretty amazing things like holding up tons of steel, and even an entire helicopter. This is simply far above anything T’Challa has been able to accomplish. However, in a straight fight, I’d give the edge to T’Challa. Unlike Steve, T’Challa has some near-impenetrable armor and a high-tech suit. He’s also got deadly claws and energy absorption. Because of this, it’s likely that the Black Panther would win in an all-out fight.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If the Infinity Gauntlet was magic and could only be created by Eitri, how did Tony Stark build two in Avengers: Endgame?
Answer: It’s not magic. The Gauntlet was simply durable enough to withstand the power of the Infinity Stones (being made of Uru). It’s incredibly difficult to get the technology to do so, but it certainly isn’t “magic” — it’s just a matter of being able to withstand the stones. While the nanotech Gauntlet wasn’t as durable as Uru, it did have the necessary power distribution to hold the power of the stones. That’s why it worked.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Could Tony Stark “figure out” magic (as in Dr. Strange’s powers) given enough time?
Answer: Absolutely not. Remember what the Ancient One says to Strange: Not even Dr. Strange can “figure out” magic completely. He (along with every other sorcerer) only scratched the surface of what the mystical arts had to offer, despite his deep knowledge given to him by ancient spell books. Tony was a man of science. Being a genius of the real world, Stark made innovations through the use of science alone. It’s what he was always good at. Even a fraction of Strange’s power would demolish every fundamental understanding of physics and quantum mechanics. It would overwhelm Stark more so than “help him figure it out”.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Would you like if the Darth Jar Jar theory was true?
Answer: Absolutely. The Darth Jar Jar theory would have been one of the greatest twists in cinematic history. And of course, that’s not to mention that it would give both merit and justice to the widely hated character. Jar Jar served no purpose, and it just doesn’t make sense for him to be where he got in the films. Seeing that he was pulling the strings the entire time would’ve done his character justice. That being said, the Darth Jar Jar theory is also certainly plausible. Let’s take a look at some evidence: He’s impossibly skilled at fighting (through pretending to be clumsy), He has been shown to tame animals after waving his hand (a common Jedi mind trick), He can jump impossibly high (Force Jump), He convinced the Senate to give Palpatine emergency powers, His eyes are Sith yellow, And he was identified as a “Jedi” by a Separatist leader.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why doesn't Tony Stark give all the Avengers Iron Man armor?
Answer: While the other answers are true in saying that (most of) the Avengers wouldn’t actually benefit from an Iron Man suit, there is another factor to consider: Time. While he is a genius, Tony doesn’t just make suits out of thin air. They were designed in his lab, where he spent every part of his free time creating. And mind you, nearly all his work went to his own suit. Having to now take on the work of building personally tailored suits for the Avengers who needed very specific modifications would be too much to do, even for Tony. He only has so much time. All of this effort just to give a bunch of people suits that they were more than powerful without is just unnecessary, and it could also backtrack innovations for Tony’s own suits and technology.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What was Tony Stark supposed to say in the press conference at the end of Ironman 1?
Answer: Well, SHIELD developed a story to help Tony cover his tracks. Agent Coulson: Here’s your alibi…you were on your yacht. We have port papers that put you in Avalon all night and sworn statements from fifty of your guests. Tony: There’s nothing about Stane. Agent Coulson: That's being handled. He's on vacation. Small aircraft have such a poor safety record. So apparently, Tony was supposed to say that he was on a private island in a yacht the night of when he fought Stane.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Given how much money he cost them, why didn't Marvel try to kill off Iron Man sooner? He was seemingly being paid almost as much as all the other Avengers combined but it doesn't seem like he's worth more than all of them.
Answer: Because Iron Man became a gold mine. Film producers like Marvel aren’t stupid. They’d never spend much on an IP that they weren’t 100% sure they’d make at least 10x more revenue from. Based on those projections, the actors are paid accordingly for their roles. Downey’s Iron Man became one of the most successful fictional characters in movie history, but this wasn’t always the case. In fact, RDJ was initially paid a modest $500,000 for his role in Iron Man because of how big of a risk the film was. It was only after Marvel’s massive success that he received an additional $50 million for the first movie. Once Iron Man became a worldwide sensation, Downey got paid the big bucks — for example, he was paid $75 million for Endgame. But with this hefty paycheck also came billions in revenue and tons of fame for the franchise. In other words, Iron Man is and will continue to always be a worthy investment to put on the big screen. It’s why, I believe, Marvel will decide to bring back Iron Man in some form (my bet being through the multiverse).

Name: Crantzer
Question: If Tony Stark trusted his fellow Avengers enough to build them suits what would they be like? Specifically I’m wondering about Captain America, Black Widow, and Hawkeye.
Answer: Let’s start with some that might just work: Captain America Steve is agile, but he does often take a number of blunt hits — it's why he often uses his shield. An Iron Man suit (perhaps nanotech to make it a bit easier to move in) would do him good. Black Widow Surprisingly enough, Natasha actually makes a suit in comics. It was light enough for her to move well enough in, and it provided her enough durability to take on threats above her paygrade. Thor Thor doesn’t necessarily need a suit, but it could increase his strength and durability. While it’s unlikely he’d use it, perhaps a backup power-absorbant suit could be good for bigger threats like Thanos. Now those who would not benefit from a suit: Hulk The guy is wildly durable and powerful already. A suit doesn’t do a damn thing besides have a high chance of breaking or pissing him off. Hawkeye Clint’s deal is that he’s stealthy and accurate. His aim is already immaculate so he doesn’t need a suit for help, and a suit would just slow him down and make him more conspicuous. He’d never use a suit. Dr. Strange Yea, no…Strange’s power is far beyond the need to use mortal metals.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Tony Stark to blame for Ultron and all the damage and destruction caused by Ultron?
Answer: Not entirely. A whole lot of people tend to forget that Banner was just as involved in building Ultron as Tony was. Wanda also played a major (yet often-overlooked) part in instilling that fear-mongering vision inside Tony’s head.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If Hela was alive in Avengers: Infinity War, would she have fought with the Avengers and Guardians against Thanos?
Answer: No, but she’d still fight him. There’s absolutely no reason for Hela to fight alongside the Avengers. Her ultimate goal was to conquer the nine realms, and they’d only stand in her way. Instead, she’d take on the Mad Titan head-on. He was too much of a threat for her — not only was Thanos trying to get the stones, but he would’ve snapped away half of Hela’s would-be kingdom. She simply would not allow that to happen. Besides, I doubt Hela would need the Avengers. The goddess of death was so powerful that even the Allfather himself couldn’t contain her power. She also decimated an awakened Thor, the entire Asgardian army, and the entire Valkyrie. Her necroswords can even cut through Uru! Had she stayed on Asgard a bit more, she’d be even more powerful than we see her in the MCU (seeing as her power grows as she is on Asgard). This version of Hela (along with her considerably-sized army and Fenris, as well as any planets she might pick up along the way) would stand a solid chance against Thanos’ army. As for Thanos himself, it’s likely that Hela has the power to take him on single-handedly as well.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Andor vs. Obi-Wan. Why did one of the shows become a flop?
Answer: Because one had great expectations. The other didn’t. Everyone expected something legendary from the Obi-Wan series. People hoped that perhaps, for the first time in a long time, Disney would make something amazing. You can’t mess up Kenobi and Vader, right? This mindset likely settled into the writers of the show — surely, simply because of the big names of the show, people would love it. It’s probably why they didn’t spend much time actually working on the writing and instead focused on the (admittedly amazing) cinematics. Andor, however, was completely different. Most fans (including myself) didn’t expect anything more than mediocre from the show. But boy, were we pleasantly surprised. Instead of expecting you to already know and love everyone in the show, Andor took the time to flesh out their characters. The show didn’t mind a slow pace for a hefty payoff. It was that “drag” of suspense and intrigue that led to such an amazing payoff in the first place. That is, of course, not to mention the absolutely brilliant cast.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who would win in a fight, Hela or Ultron?
Answer: Physically, Hela would win. Her power is above that of gods, and was even too much for the Allfather himself to contain. Her necroswords can also cut Uru. So yes, she’d be able to cut through and/or destroy the android. However, the problem is that Ultron transcends the physical realm. See, the whole reason Ultron was so dangerous in Age of Ultron was because he managed to infiltrate the internet. It’s what gave him the ability to remotely control the entire world. Even if Hela destroyed his body, she couldn’t destroy Ultron’s essence. He would simply sit in the internet until he made a new body. Perhaps he’d even learn from his mistakes and make a more powerful one as time progressed.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How could Frigga tell Thor was from the future?
Answer: Well, according to Frigga it’s because she has greater vision through sorcery. Of course, anyone with two eyes (no offense, Thor) could easily realize that their one-eyed, fatter, hobo-dressed son was not their own. But what the average person would not be able to realize is that the person is from another timeline.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why does Hank Pym hate Tony Stark?
Answer: Because he hated Tony’s father. Hank and Howard Stark were colleagues. Both were brilliant minds who revolutionized the world with their technology, but Howard wanted to take Hank’s Pym Particles and use them for manufacturing. This was not something Hank ever wanted to do after he lost his wife during a mission using the Pym Particles. Howard didn’t respect that choice and decided to instead go behind Hank’s back and try to make it. Suffice it to say, Howard failed—and their relationship soured. So what does this have to do with Tony? Well, similar to his father, Tony was an innovator who used his greatest works for manufacturing and/or profit. As far as Hank was concerned, Tony was just like his father (which wasn’t necessarily untrue). That is why Hank refused to call Stark (or any other Avenger) to deal with the Yellowjacket threat. Scott: I think our first move should be calling the Avengers. Hank: I spent half my life trying to keep this technology out of the hands of a Stark. I’m sure as hell not going to hand deliver it to one now.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If Tom Holland's MCU Spider-Man turned evil, what Avenger, if any, could stop him?
Answer: Let’s start with the obvious ones: Some close calls: Everyone else not mentioned should die to Peter fairly easily. Peter is incredibly powerful, and could absolutely hold his own against a lot of the Avengers. But still, many are around his power, if not more so.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Zemo kill the other 5 Winter Soldiers?
Answer: Because he’s not completely evil. You have to understand Zemo’s end goal: to end the Avengers by destroying them from the inside. The reason wasn’t for world domination or personal glory — it was simply because they lacked accountability for the damage they caused. Killing the Winter Soldiers was to lure Cap and Tony to the secret base. However, because of how much of a danger to the general public they posed, Zemo decided to kill two birds with one stone by killing the Winter Soldiers before they could wreak havoc. Zemo wasn’t inherently a bad guy — in fact, he seemed to show regret for the collateral damage he caused. He was simply a misguided and heartbroken father and husband. He lost everything, and now he had nothing to lose. You can’t really understand that kind of loss unless you are a husband or father yourself.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What Marvel villain would be more likely to exist in real life (kingpin aside)?
Answer: Definitely Justin Hammer. He’s almost too relatable. An overly ambitious (yet just as incompetent) mega-billionaire striving to seem like a tech genius, who also happens to make shady deals to get rid of the competition? Sounds kinda familiar…

Name: Crantzer
Question: How well were the Jedi known around the Galaxy before Order 66?
Answer: They weren’t very well-known at all. The Republic only really ever assisted the main inner planets. Those in the mid-rim or outer region rarely saw government interference on their planets (and thus many of them were rampant with all kinds of unlawful anarchy and corruption). Thus, the vast majority of planets have never seen a Jedi before. In fact, because of how little the Jedi actually traveled around the Galaxy (instead focusing on core worlds), most common people believed the Jedi didn’t even exist. Han Solo was one of those people.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How did Thanos know Iron Man's name in Avengers: Infinity War?
Answer: Because he knew all about Earth. Remember what Ronan said in Captain Marvel: [Ronan arrives on Earth] Ronan: Deploy ballistic warheads. [Captain Marvel destroys the warheads from below] Ronan: That’s impossible…C-53 doesn’t have a defense system advanced enough to destroy our warheads. Intergalactic empires like the Kree had information on Earth — so much so that they had specific knowledge of Earth’s defenses and even had a name for it (C-53). Mind you, this is decades prior to the events of The Avengers and Infinity War. Before Thanos launched his major assault on Earth in 2012, he likely did some research on the planet. Clearly, he has the technology to do so (seeing as the Kree did, and the Kree were loyal to Thanos at the time). Whether it was before or after his failed attack, Thanos would have, at some point, taken a look at the Earth. And when he did, he’d find that one name would be very famous and powerful there: Stark. From buildings to expos to satellites, Stark had his name plastered all over the world. It’s no stretch to imagine that Thanos heard of Tony in his research of the planet and that the guy who threw a nuke at his Chitauri Command Center was the same guy who built a suit of armor around the world. That’s how Thanos knew the name Stark.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why does Doctor Strange show Tony one finger in Avengers: Endgame?
Answer: There’s actually an interesting theory about what Strange actually meant. Let’s look back at the conversation Tony has with his dad when he travels back in time to get the Tesseract: Upon meeting his father, Tony had an awkward “handshake” with Howard because he only held one of his fingers while Tony went for a handshake. Because of this mismatch, Tony ended up pulling Howard’s hand instead of shaking it. Howard then makes this remark: The theory goes that, knowing all of the aspects of the timeline in which they one, Strange knew that Tony would have this awkward intro with his dad. On the battlefield, Strange then reminds Tony of this crucial memory: Shake it, don’t pull it. Once Tony understood this, he shook the stones instead of pulling the Gauntlet, which eventually took off the stones and gave him the advantage.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What fictional character do you feel the most sorry for or pity?
Answer: Luis from Ant-Man. Luis never deserved what he got in his life. He spent years in jail for petty theft and then became friends with Scott in jail. He was Scott’s ride-or-die forever since then. Then by the time he got out of jail, Luis lost everyone he loved. But despite all of that, he always managed to look on the bright side.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What have you noticed in Zack Snyder's Justice League that most people have not?
Answer: The Flash was ready to phase Superman’s attack. Notice what Barry does right before Clark is about to laser him: This same gesture was what Barry made to phase through the blast in the final fight against Steppenwolf. This raise of hand is something that activates Barry’s phasing ability. So the fact that he did it right before Superman was going to laser him makes it clear that he was about to phase. As an honorable sidenote, Barry’s fight with Superman also contains an easter egg referencing Ben Parker.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who would win, Mikhail Tal or Magnus Carlsen?
Answer: Magnus would crush Tal, but not for the reasons you think. Tal was a legendary player. Even calling him brilliant doesn’t do him justice — he holds both the first and second longest unbeaten streaks in chess history. So then, how can Magnus win so thoroughly against Tal? Well, the answer’s simple: Magnus was born in the age of computers. Unlike Tal’s era of high-level guesswork, a computer can now tell you what the objectively best move is. Before, the best move would simply be common consensus. But today, even the greatest grandmasters often doubt their moves because they know the computer can always find what they can’t. With this day of superhuman-advanced chess analysis, there also came several new theories and openings. Combining this with the fact that (despite chess being a far larger sport than before) Magnus is still crushing even in today’s era, it is abundantly clear that Tal would stand no chance against the five-time World Champion.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Thor love Jane?
Answer: Because Jane treated him as her equal. All throughout his life, Thor has went throughout the cosmos outclassing the most powerful of warriors. He and the rest of Asgard were revered across the universe for their power and benevolence. However, the story was very different with Jane. From the moment they met, it was almost as if Jane was the one teaching/helping Thor. He felt, for the first time, that someone wasn’t attracted to him for his power or fame, but because of who he was as a person. Thor likely never experienced that kind of genuine, mutual relationship before. That’s what led him to be attracted to her. But of course, that’s all not to mention that she’s a brilliant scientist with supermodel looks.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What small Marvel Cinematic Universe moments do you wish people talked more about?
Answer: The fact that Tony adapts his suits by learning from his mistakes. Back in Iron Man 2, Tony’s suit got damaged by electricity. So, he later made it power absorbent. In Iron Man 3, Tony got stranded in the cold. So, he later added heaters to Peter’s suit. In Civil War, Ant-Man slipped between the gaps in Tony’s armor. So, he made it into nanotech, where there are no gaps. In Civil War, Tony wasn’t fast enough to save Rhodey from his fall. So, he added extra turbo blasters to go much faster.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who is the most inconsistent Marvel character?
Answer: Oh, this one’s easy. The most inconsistent MCU character has to go to Loki, by a long shot. This is the same guy who: Tried to kill Thor numerous times over the course of thousands of years, Almost eradicated his own race, Joined one of the most genocidal people in the universe to help destroy earth, Decimated New York, Stabbed Thor again, Claimed no remorse for his crimes, Stabbed Odin in the back by banishing him and taking the throne, Stabbed Thor in the back again by not helping him on Sakaar, And stabbed Thor in the back AGAIN by stealing the Tesseract. Pretty awful stuff, right? Well, in the Loki series (which is fantastic, by the way), Marvel decided to make a new spin on Loki. His character development — which very gradually happened over the course of 10 years — happened in one instance by watching a film. Essentially, Loki (the one during the attack on New York) watched how his life would play out with his “redemption arc”, despite him still backstabbing everyone around him in every single movie. Now, this guy who had no problem eradicating entire planets has suddenly turned into the hero of the multiverse. This new Loki now spent all of his efforts saving others and even spent centuries studying physics in order to be able to protect the multiverse. Funnily enough, he was even offered the greatest throne one could ever ask for (by Kang), but declined! And mind you, this was just a few weeks (at most) prior to him trying to conquer earth! This really felt out of character for the egotistical, backstabbing character we all love to turn into a benevolent and righteous man who defends others rather than taking personal glory.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Generally speaking, how strong is a 1,700 rating in chess?
Answer: Pretty damn good. Professional chess streamer Andrea Botez, who had an elo of 1714 back in 2018, and is currently at 1858. The average global chess elo is between 700—1100. The vast majority of global players will fall into that category. 1700 is far beyond that of the average chess player. The USCF places players with an elo ranging from 1700–1799 as being in the 87.61th percentile. And mind you, that’s only including registered players with the USCF! The real number of casual players who never registered will be much lower. For example, you’d be in the top 1% of chess players on chess.com. 1700 definitely isn’t professional level, but it is a very good rating in general. You won’t be beating IMs or GMs anytime soon, but thankfully most chess players aren’t.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if a chess player had a 4,000 Elo rating?
Answer: It’s impossible. The peak of human chess intelligence in history is considerably below 2900 Elo. Even the strongest chess engine to date (Stockfish 16) is at an estimated 3634 Elo. While Stockfish may seem not too far from 4000, it absolutely is. There comes a point in Elo that even a 25–50 point difference means one engine can consistently beat another. Jumping almost 400 points from 3634 to 4000 would crush even the highest version of Stockfish. I won’t say computers will never be able to reach 4000, but it is absolutely impossible for a human to even come close to doing so. To be able to be that advanced would mean you have a brain with processing power exponentially more than a supercomputer. In that case, you’re better off curing cancer.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Excluding Thanos, which Marvel film had the most universe threatening villain?
Answer: Actually, Thanos is nowhere near the most powerful MCU villain. That would be this guy: Dormammu, Destroyer of Worlds Dormammu is literally a multiversal threat and consumer of worlds. His power was so great that even mystic beings like the Ancient One couldn’t stand a chance against him. In fact, the combined power of all mystic arts can’t even kill him — the best they can do is prevent him from destroying everything. Petty, tiny beings like Thanos would be no problem for him. Some other honorable mentions (all of which are more powerful than the Mad Titan) include: Ego, Surtur, Hela, and of course Kang.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In Avengers: Endgame, how did Tony Stark invent time travel in a single evening?
Answer: It wasn’t overnight. Just because the movie skips to Tony at night doesn’t mean it was the same day he had the conversation with Steve, Natasha, and Scott. Tony remarks that he wants to run “one last sim”, implying that he had been running numerous before. Tony also didn’t come up with time travel from scratch. Stark came up with the idea of time travel through a significant head start — Pym Particles. These bad boys are arguably the most advanced piece of technology ever developed by humans (yes, including the Iron Man suits). It was absolutely revolutionary to change how they viewed time and space. It was only through using the template of Hank Pym’s particles that Tony could even scratch the surface of time travel. Without it, he wouldn’t have figured it out.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did Odin meet the Eternals?
Answer: Oh, yes. Notice what Kingo says in Eternals: Clearly, the Eternals had some sort of connection with Asgard and its royal family. Perhaps their relationships even go back to Odin’s days of conquest with Hela. It’s also very likely that Odin was aware of or even met the Celestials at some point.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if Captain America preformed the snap instead of Iron Man? What would change and how?
Answer: It would not go as well as you think. The main reason Tony managed to hold the power of the stones as long as he did was because of his seriously durable armor. It was able to absorb the Power Stone at one point, and it was slowly being destroyed by the Infinity Gauntlet. Look back at Tony’s snap: Notice how the energy is being distributed throughout the suit? It’s because it’s taking in the lion’s share of the energy. That’s the only reason Tony wasn’t immediately fried. Steve is different. The guy is only a bit more than peak human performance. He doesn’t have Infinity Stone durability, nor does he have armor. Because of this, Cap would get incinerated almost immediately after putting on the Gauntlet — it’s not made for mortals like him.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In your opinion, which villain in the Marvel Universe had the greatest origin story?
Answer: The greatest villain story is actually not by a villain. It’s Luis. More so than many villain arcs, this man had every reason to become a villain. He lost everything and everyone close to him. And yet, he kept a positive attitude and always looked on the bright side of things. He even risked his freedom to save Scott.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Captain America refer to Tony as “Earth’s best defender” even though there are much more powerful Avengers than Iron Man?
Answer: The same reason Thanos respected Tony more than anyone else: because power doesn’t just come from physical strength. See, Thanos knew where true power lay — in the mind. Tony was a mere human, but through his genius and dedication, he managed to build something so powerful that it could bring gods to their knees. Tony was relentless, even in certain death. He, more than any other Avenger, knew how to adapt and strike back hard. He never gave up and never backed down on the very principle that he was Earth’s first and last line of defense. Steve knew Tony more than most people did. He knew just how powerful Tony truly was when he put his mind to something. He even developed Vision, who was by far the most powerful Avenger! And unlike either Hulk or Thor, Tony invested everything in Earth’s protection. He’d stop at nothing to do what had to be done. Hulk hid away the moment he got beat. In contrast, Tony never backed down, even when faced with certain defeat.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If Iron Man had prep time (like Batman), could he defeat all the enemies in the MCU?
Answer: No. While he could beat most, there are a number of MCU villains that Tony has no chance of beating (prep time or not): Kaecilius Tony knows almost nothing about the mystic arts. Kaecilius was a man who was incredibly formidable by drawing power from the dark dimension. While he might hold off for some time, the only thing a guy like Kaecilius really has to do is put Tony in a mirror dimension and leave him there. Dormammu This one is, I hope, obvious. Dormammu is a consumer of multiverses, and superpowered beings like Dr. Strange and the Ancient One stand no chance against him. There’s no way in hell Tony doesn’t get fried to a crisp. Ego The guy is literally a planet that was minutes away from consuming almost every biological planet in the universe. His powers were so great that the only person who stood a chance against him was his son Star-Lord, who had his powers. Hela Thor in his awakened state stood no chance against his sister — and neither did the Asgardian army (warriors who had superhuman strength). Even Odin in his prime couldn’t contain her power. Tony dies easily. Surtur (Peak Form) This one should also be obvious. Hela stood no chance against the flaming beast, and neither would Tony.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who's suit is more advanced, Iron Man's or Black Panther's?
Answer: I’m quite shocked by some of the answers here. Tony’s nanotech is arguably the most advanced piece of technology in the entire MCU, and it is far beyond T’Challa’s Black Panther tech. By Infinity War, Tony’s suit is basically magic. It’s millennia ahead of its time and has tons of hidden weaponry like firethrowers and missiles. It also has blasters able to go at rocket speeds and self-healing properties for near-fatal wounds. And mind you, this is all held inside a coaster-sized chest piece. T’Challa’s suit is nothing but an exoskeleton of vibranium. Sure, it has nanotech — but that’s nothing Tony doesn’t already have. Let’s put it in perspective: T’Challa’s suit (along with his superhuman strength) had a hard time against dozens of ravagers, and he lasted a whopping three seconds against Thanos himself. Meanwhile, Tony’s suit not only survived in space and killed Maw (Thanos’ most powerful child), but he also went toe-to-toe with the Mad Titan, who at the time had four Infinity Stones! He’s also the only one to make Thanos bleed. Tony’s suit is exponentially more advanced and more powerful than T’Challa’s has ever been. While it is true that Wakanda itself may be more technologically advanced than the rest of the world in general, this has nothing to do with Tony. Stark is another level of genius, it’s why he is legendarily known as “Earth’s best defender”.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if Tony Stark never died?
Answer: It would change a lot more than you think. Had Tony never died and instead survived the snap, the most obvious effect would be that he would continue being there for his family and watching Morgan grow up. He’d likely retire from being Iron Man (seeing as he had a family) and instead continue living similarly as he did prior to Endgame. However, there is more than just that. Being retired from everything else and prioritizing family, Tony would likely still give Peter the reigns as he did in Far From Home. Things would then continue similarly as they did in Far From Home, except for one caveat: Peter’s identity leak would be different. Had Tony been there while Peter was in hot water, he would’ve backed him up completely. Stark would give Peter complete and utter legal protection while also trying to keep Peter’s innocence. In fact, if push ever came to shove, it’s likely that Tony would even accept responsibility for a majority of Peter’s crimes to get him off the hook. This would prevent Peter from ever needing to go to Dr. Strange, which would also prevent the multiversal issues of No Way Home. In the end, Peter wouldn’t have lost his girlfriend and mentor (Happy) like in the original timeline and instead would continue to be a Stark-defended and maybe controversial hero to some — but a hero nonetheless.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who is the most broken character in the MCU?
Answer: While there are a lot of great answers here, I’m surprised no one has mentioned Peter Parker. The guy has experienced more pain and loss than most others in the MCU. Peter lost his parents at a young age, and then lost his uncle Ben which made him live with his single Aunt May. He then lost his high school crush because her dad tried to kill him. Then his father figure and mentor — the only man who ever believed in him — died in front of him. Later, the entire world falsely accused him of being a criminal and destroyed both his and his friends’ lives. Then, after an effort to undo that, he allowed Green Goblin to kill his Aunt May — the only parental figure he had left. And in an effort to undo everything else, Peter lost the love of his life (MJ), his best friend (Ned), and Happy. Peter quite literally lost everyone and everything he ever loved. At the point of No Way Home, no one even knew who he was. At least characters like Thor and Natasha (who have very heartbreaking and broken lives as well) had connections and people who cared about them. But now, Peter has nothing.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How did Captain America call Mjolnir? Was he faking like he could not lift Mjolnir in the first Avengers film?
Answer: Oh, yes. Notice again the scene of Cap “lifting” Mjolnir in Age of Ultron: See that little *creak* Mjolnir made? Thor definitely saw it, and Cap felt it. It was at that moment that Cap realized he could lift Mjolnir. There’s no way, even with his strength, he could’ve made the immovable hammer move like that — people of far greater strength have tried and failed. Cap simply chose not to lift the hammer, so as to save Thor’s reputation. He only eventually took it when it was necessary.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are the best MCU theories you've heard?
Answer: Odin once had all six Infinity Stones. We see in Thor: Ragnarok that there is a fake Infinity Gauntlet in Odin’s treasure vault. The reason Hela knew this was fake is not only because Odin had the real ones at one point, but Hela helped him get them. Odin had a dark past before Thor and Frigga. We know that prior to Hela’s conquest, Odin was a conquering warrior alongside his daughter who swept through the nine realms, looting from other worlds. The theory goes that while traveling the cosmos, Odin took the Infinity Stones from all around the universe and held them in his vault. There is also proof that he used the stones. One prevailing theory is that Odin actually used the Soul Stone to give Heimdall his powers of being able to see every soul in the universe. The colors of his eyes conveniently match the Soul Stone as well. Odin likely got the Soul Stone by perhaps sacrificing someone he loved — maybe even Hela’s mother (which would explain why we know nothing about her). We also know that Odin eventually got a change of heart — he decided it was better to maintain peace between the nine realms rather than conquer it. Because of this, he banished Hela (who wouldn’t stop fighting) for the rest of his life. After this, Odin eventually dispersed the Infinity Stones all throughout the nine realms so that such a power couldn’t easily be taken from his vault (and maybe so he wouldn’t be tempted to use it again). This would explain why things like the power stone were in a relatively easy-to-steal place, and why the tesseract was given to random people in Norway (only for Red Skull to find it later on). We know very little about who Odin was before Thor was born. But as far as we know, he was an overly ambitious man who put personal power and glory above all else. Taking the Infinity Stones would very much be something he’d do. Odin likely secretly discarded the Stones later on and just lied to say that he still had them in order to keep instilling fear within the universe about his power.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Vision call himself “I Am” in the Avengers movie?
Answer: There are some answers here that think Vision sees himself as a Christ-like figure (seeing as Jesus calls Himself “I Am” in the Bible). However, this couldn’t be further from the truth. Vision didn’t know who he was. He didn’t know whether he was good, evil, or something else — he questioned his morals constantly. Thinking himself to be a morally good, outstanding, and deity-like figure would be contradictory to everything else he says about himself. What Vision means is that all he knows of himself is that he presently exists. It’s like the famous Descartes philosophy: “I think, therefore I am”. Similarly, despite all the doubts Vision has of himself, he finds that the one thing he can’t doubt is his existence. To him, that is the only truth of his essence.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if Captain America/Steve Rogers was born in Germany?
Answer: Things would turn out much worse. The entire point that HYDRA didn’t have a Super Soldier during Cap’s time was because they didn’t have the serum. But in a hypothetical where they had the serum before the US did, things would be really bad. Steve helped turn the tide of World War II. Having him on the side of the Germans would’ve been the other way around. In the end, it’s likely that perhaps the Nazis may have been able to win the war and overthrow the United States. This would have far more ripple effects than simply the change of world governments. Had the Nazis won (with the help of Cap), leading scientists like Howard Stark may have been either subjected to creating great weapons of destruction, or killed. This would be the environment Tony stark grows up in. If Howard decided to not die and instead work for HYDRA, Tony would likely continue the family’s legacy and build even greater weapons for them. This would mean he never becomes the Iron Man we all know about today. And, of course, that would probably mean that the universe’s greatest sacrifice would never take place.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are your thoughts on the Darth Jar Jar theory?
Answer: It’s entirely possible. Let’s take a look at some interesting evidence: He has been shown to tame animals after waving his hand (a common Jedi mind trick), He’s impossibly skilled at fighting (through the means of acting clumsy), He has jumped impossibly high (something you can do with Force jump), He convinced the entire Senate to give a Sith Lord emergency powers, His eyes are Sith yellow, And he was identified as a “Jedi” by a Separatist leader. There are so many nuanced clues pointing to Binks being a Jedi. In fact, it is a prevailing and strong theory (through heavy implications by the man himself) that George Lucas originally intended for him to be a secret Sith, but he eventually scrapped the idea after the immense hate of the character. Had he continued on with it, watching Binks expose his true self would’ve been a sight to see.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who would win, Winter Soldier vs. Batman?
Answer: I’m surprised by a lot of the answers here. Batman is no doubt an excellent assassin and fighter, but the Winter Soldier is something else. He managed to hold off Falcon, Black Widow, and Cap all at once and then disappeared. He’s the very definition of a professional superassassin. Unfortunately, Batman is out of his depth here. He doesn’t have the superhuman abilities of the Winter Soldier. While he may have more gadgets, it’d be difficult to beat the very formidable assassin. Eventually, after a tough fight (seeing as Batman’s gadgets may spare him for a time), the Winter Soldier should win.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are the requirements to lift Thor's hammer?
Answer: The requirement is actually quite vague. What the hell does it mean to “be worthy”? Could it mean to be pure of heart? Well, pretty much every time Thor is seen with the hammer later on, he is far from a humble guy. Does it mean to be a good ruler? Then surely, people like Tony (one of the leaders of the greatest superhero team in the universe) should be able to lift it. Does it mean to just be a good person? Well, Vision wasn’t even a person and was able to lift it! The requirements to lift Mjolnir make quite literally no sense. The criteria for being “worthy” is entirely open to interpretation, which may be the whole point. Perhaps Mjolnir has a mind of its own and just decides who is worthy and who isn’t. It changed his mind about Jane.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What prevents Loki from hypnotizing Tony Stark by using the mind stone in ‘The Avengers’?
Answer: Well, we know that Howard Stark developed the first arc reactor. We also know that he had studied quite a bit of the Tesseract during his lifetime. It’s possible that Howard used technology and/or substances from the Tesseract to develop the arc reactor. Both were immensely high-energy forms of power that were vastly ahead of their time. Because of this, it’s likely that Howard’s potential usage of the Tesseract to develop the arc reactor led to a cancelled-out reaction when the stone touches it.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How much does Thor's hammer weigh?
Answer: In 1991, Marvel issued a Thor’s Hammer trading card that confirmed the weight of Mjolnir to be 42.3 pounds. Of course, the weight drastically changes to (essentially) infinity for those who aren’t worthy to lift it.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Groot use his arm for the axe's handle in Infinity War's?
Answer: Because nothing else was left. The scene was very dramatic. Thor was helplessly on the edge of death after taking the full force of a star, and Eitri was desperately looking for Stormbreaker’s handle. As far as we know, he never found it. At that point, Groot realized he needed to get his act together. He wasn’t doing a damn thing while everyone else was literally trying to save the universe. So, he decided to take his eyes off his device for a whopping 15 seconds and make a handle with his arm. And sure enough, it worked!

Name: Crantzer
Question: Would Count Dooku and Asajj Ventress defeat Emperor Palpatine together in a fight when Darth Maul and Savage Oppress could not?
Answer: Contrary to popular belief, I’d say yes. Dooku is criminally underrated in his skill and Force power. He has been shown to take on two of the most powerful Jedi effortlessly on numerous occasions. He also managed to go toe-to-toe with Yoda (the second most powerful Force user in history). Ventress was no slouch, either. In fact, she was so powerful that Palpatine sensed her powers were too strong for Dooku to have as an apprentice. So, he made Dooku get rid of her. Had she progressed in Dooku’s training for a few more years, I do believe they’d be a good match against the powerful Sith Lord.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Thor stronger than Ultron?
Answer: In the MCU, no. Contrary to the comics, Thor is horrendously nerfed on the big screen. Because of this, his strength and size pale in comparison to his comic counterpart. This was why Ultron managed to take on all of the Avengers — for the sake of the movie. In reality with Ultron’s suit, someone like Hulk or Thor would’ve been more than enough to decimate the android. But in the movies, there were even moments when Ultron had Thor within his grasp.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Can Superman get fat like Thor?
Answer: He can, and he did. A Silver Age comic revealed that while he doesn’t get fat from overeating Earth food, Clark can become overweight by Red Kryptonite. In one issue, a local milk factory exposed Red Kryptonite radiation to its products. Because of this, Kent gained a ton of weight.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What was the most one-sided fight in Marvel Comics (not movies)?
Answer: Probably the fight between God Emperor Doom and Thanos. In this issue, Doom inherited the powers of The Beyonders (the most powerful of beings in the multiverse). The Mad Titan stood no chance of even trying to stop him. Another honorable mention is Thor’s discipline at the hands of his father. Suffice it to say, Odin wasn’t father of the year.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who was the better fighter: Boba or Jango Fett?
Answer: Jango Fett, but not by a lot. The guy managed to go toe-to-toe against one of the most powerful Jedi of all time (Obi-Wan). He was also hand-picked for cloning to create the most powerful army in the Galaxy. But this wasn’t the only time Jango fought Jedi — in fact, he even managed to kill two Jedi with both his bare hands and a rock! The only reason Jango lost so quickly against Mace (the second best duelist in the Order) was because his jetpack was jammed at the time. That being said, Boba is no slouch either. While he has taken on high-value targets, Jedi were more of Jango’s specialty. In fact, the only time he even fought a Jedi was a less-than-competent Luke. In that sense, I’d reckon that Boba’s father has the upper hand in terms of prowess. The guy is criminally underrated.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Will Grogu stick with Din Djarin or become a Jedi?
Answer: Probably both. You have to understand, Grogu has a far longer lifespan than his adoptive dad. Before Grogu even starts looking like a preteen, Din will be dead. Because of this, it’s likely that perhaps (following Din’s death) Grogu will go back to Luke’s Jedi Temple and become a Jedi again. Unfortunately, seeing as Kylo ended up destroying the temple (decades after The Mandalorian), it is a common and plausible theory that Grogu died alongside everyone else at the Temple.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who would win in a fight, Jedi Dooku or Sith Dooku?
Answer: Notice what Yoda tells Dooku: Now look at what Dooku tells Yoda: Dooku had progressed exponentially in power over time after tapping into the dark side. He knew it, and Yoda sensed it. This increase in power not only came from more experience but also through the forbidden Force techniques a Sith is allowed to learn, like Force Lightning.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who would win, Cad Bane vs Din Djarin?
Answer: Din is out of his depth here. Bane is an absolute menace. He was the most formidable bounty hunter in the Galaxy and managed was feared by all who heard his name. His clients were almost all high-profile, much of which were of the Separatist and Galactic Empire. The bounty hunter has even outclassed Jedi on occasion. While Mando is a great bounty hunter himself, he’s not a legend in the industry like Bane or Boba Fett. He is skilled, but he’s not that skilled. Had the two ever crossed paths, it wouldn’t end well for the Mandalorian.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What was the most selfish act committed by Iron Man?
Answer: When Tony thought about refusing to time travel for the sake of his family. Pepper: A lot of people [weren’t as lucky as us]. Tony: I can’t help everybody. Pepper: Sorta seems like you can. Tony: Not if I stop. I can put a pin on it right now and stop. To be clear, I get it — I completely understand Tony’s thoughts here. Thanos happened five years ago, and since then he has gotten through that trauma and started a family. It’s not easy to just leave his wife and kid alone to pursue this time travel dream that may not even work. That being said, Tony was still thinking about himself here. Ever since his character arc as Iron Man, that’s the last thing he did — care about himself. This sudden change went to show just how much the events of Infinity War affected him.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Where was Iron Man during Winter Soldier?
Answer: Tony actually makes an appearance in The Winter Soldier. We know that during the entire conflict with HYDRA, Tony was actually at Stark Tower in New York. He was shown there in live footage, seeing as he was one of millions of HYDRA targets. So, what exactly was Tony doing at Stark Tower? Well, one can only guess, but it’s likely that he was helping repair the tower and city after Loki’s attempted conquest. This was only two years after the events of The Avengers, and the damage to the city was quite extensive. It’s also entirely possible that Tony was working on other projects. He told banner in The Avengers that they had a number of cool projects going on there. I’d like to think that perhaps Tony was starting research on building Ultron, or perhaps even the Hulkbuster suit.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if Thor snap instead of Iron Man?
Answer: Things would turn out much better for everyone. Thor is arguably the most powerful Avenger of them all. He’s also the most experienced in battle. We also know that while he did struggle, Hulk had no life-threatening damage from the stones, but instead got a crispy burn on his arm. Thor is also a very tough cookie. He’s taken the force of a dying star on occasion. At worst, Thor would’ve suffered severe damage on his arm from the snap. And even that could easily be fixed. He already has a robotic eye, what’s another artificial body part? Of course, the biggest problem was timing — Tony was the only one who could get to the stones in time. It’s why he made that split-second decision that cost him his life. Unlike folks like Thor or Hulk, Tony decided to take the power of the stones despite knowing it’d kill him. That’s what’s called bravery, and it makes Tony’s sacrifice all the more powerful than Thor’s could’ve ever been.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did Darth Vader have any chance of overthrowing the Emperor by himself?
Answer: No. Palpatine had made a contingency plan in case Vader were to act up — he made Vader’s suit susceptible to electricity so that he could be neutralized quickly. In fact, he’s used this attack before against his apprentice in order to show him the true extent of his power. However, there is another reason it’d be hard for Vader to overthrow Palpatine. Palpatine’s power extends far beyond just the Force. He was the most powerful man in the Empire, and he had eyes & ears everywhere. In fact, the Royal Guards (given to all powerful people in the Empire, including Vader) were personal eyes and ears of the Emperor. The moment Vader even started the idea of plotting against the Emperor, he’d know. Not only this, but Palpatine was also immensely influential. It’s highly unlikely that most (if any) of the current Empire would simply allow Vader to assume control after overthrowing Palpatine. Some within the Empire even outclassed Vader. While it seems like a good idea in theory, overthrowing the Emperor just wasn’t realistic. There were a number of logistic and physical limitations to accomplishing such a goal. It’s part of why Vader desperately tried to get Luke to join him — because he knew he couldn’t do it alone.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Was Din Djarin's armour better than Boba Fett's?
Answer: In terms of durability? Absolutely. Din wore a full body of pure beskar. It covered a good portion of his body, making him near-impenetrable to both blaster fire and tough hits. Suffice it to say, he’s very durable. But in terms of efficiency? Probably not. Din’s armor was heavier than Boba’s, so it restricted his movements quite a bit. Carrying around pure beskar is no joke. Boba likes to be swift and precise, so having armor that gives him good movement is imperative. In the end, it all depends on fighting style. Mando has the perfect armor for who he is, and so does Boba. Now, if you’re asking which armor is cooler, that’s a different story. Call me old-fashioned, but I prefer the rustic, wild-west look of Boba’s armor more than the sleek (and admittedly very cool) design of Mando.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In Avengers: Endgame, at the end, why did old Steve refuse to tell Sam how his life went with Peggy? What’s wrong with telling Sam what happened?
Answer: Because that time was his. Since he was a young man, Steve was a guy who always put his life before others. He sacrificed his own life and well-being on numerous occasions for others, and even gave up his freedom for his friend. What Cap had with Peggy was different. Up until that point, Cap lived for others. Now, he lived for himself. The time he had with his beloved was something both he and she cherished — it was an intimate, beautiful time. Because of this, Steve decided to keep that time to himself rather than “gloating” about it to Sam. It just goes to show just how much of a gentleman he truly is.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What allowed Groot to pick up Stormbreaker in Infinity War?
Answer: This is a very simple answer that a lot of people don’t understand: You don’t need to be worthy to lift Stormbreaker! Unlike Mjolnir, Stormbreaker was never enchanted by the forefathers to only be held by the “worthy”. It was simply a powerfully forged weapon with near-indestructible properties. We see numerous people lift Stormbreaker, including Groot and Thanos. You’d be surprised how many people forget this fact.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How was Thanos able to destroy Captain America’s shield?
Answer: While we don’t know exactly what Thanos’ sword is made of (a common theory being enchanted Uru), we do know that he was a destroyer and conqueror of many planets. It’s not a stretch to think that he found some formidable metal on one planet that happened to be stronger than Vibranium, and then used that for his sword. Vibranium has also never been stated to be the strongest metal in the universe. While it is very durable and the strongest metal on Earth, there are trillions of other planets. Chances are that at least one might have something close if not better to Vibranium. And as a side note, Corvus Glaive also had a similar metal (perhaps the same as Thanos’ sword), seeing as he managed to stab Vision’s vibranium body. Remember, Thanos was able to face Mjolnir, Stormbreaker, Cap’s shield, and Tony’s nanotech with the sword. Suffice it to say, it can handle quite a bit. So why was Thanos able to destroy Cap’s shield? Because vibranium isn’t indestructible, his sword is likely to have been a stronger material.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if Captain America saved Bucky Barnes from falling down from the HYDRA train in Captain America: The First Avenger (2011 film)?
Answer: It would change much more than you think. The most obvious effect of Bucky being saved from his fall is that he would’ve lived. Because of this, he likely would’ve died of old age before Steve came back from ice. HYDRA would then have to find a replacement for the Winter Soldier, which wouldn’t be impossible (seeing as they already had numerous contenders ahead of Bucky). However, there is one aspect of Bucky being alive that would change Steve and the MCU: Civil War. The whole reason Steve was an outlaw and went off the grid was because of Bucky. The entire time, he was just trying to protect his friend. That’s why he went as far as he did and even fought Tony. One could argue that Steve still would’ve fought the Accords because of personal belief, but it’s important to note that he was actually close to signing it as long as there were safeguards in place. Putting Bucky out of the equation, I believe, would’ve made that decision a lot easier for him. Regardless of whether he became a fugitive or not, Steve and Tony would’ve remained friends because Bucky would never have killed Tony’s parents. And with this, they’d be on much better terms. Because of these better terms, the Avengers would have been a lot more united upon Thanos’ arrival. The only reason that Earth lost as quickly as it did was that the Avengers were scattered, a lot of them outlaws. Had Steve and the rest never gone off the grid, it’s unlikely that Corvus Glaive would’ve got as close as he did to Vision to stab him. And even if he did, the team would much more efficiently be able to get to Wakanda and get Vision patched up before Thanos’ arrival. And we all know how OP Vision in his prime can get. In the end, things very likely would have worked out much better for Earth, especially during Thanos’ attack. Infinity War may have even been a success. It all really comes down to Civil War. Tony (somewhat rightfully) blamed Cap for not being there, and because of that they lost. I agree with Tony. With a united front, they would’ve been much more effective and might’ve even won. Besides, they were close even in the main timeline.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If Anakin loved Padme, why wouldn't he run away with her?
Answer: Because he thought it was best to rule with her. At the point of RoTS, Anakin stopped underestimating himself. He truly believed he was the greatest source of power in the universe, and that everything he willed would come to pass. Why then, with all this power, should he run away with Padme and live sedentary lives in some remote place? Instead, Anakin believed that what was right in front of him (and what was best for his family) was to rule the Galaxy as one. He thought it was so blatantly obvious and that Padme would surely see the bigger picture. But she didn’t. So, he snapped.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How does Captain America know how to find Wakanda in Avengers: Infinity War?
Answer: Because he had been there before. After the final fight of Civil War, T’Challa met up with Steve and Bucky, telling them that he would help find Zemo and give aid to Bucky. He also said he’d contact them again. Sure enough, at the end of the movie, T’Challa took them to Wakanda so Bucky could be treated. Thus, by the time Infinity War rolled around, Steve already knew where Wakanda was and was welcome there any time.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Which Marvel characters do fans believe deserve more love and screen time in the MCU films?
Answer: Definitely Jimmy Woo. The guy is absolutely amazing in every film, and he’s played by the very lovable Randall Park. Every time I see his character on the big screen is always a delight. He’s funny but not overly annoying (like Korg), and he did contribute quite a bit to every part he was in — especially in WandaVision. I’d love to see more of Woo in the future, because he seems like a great guy with a lot of potential within the MCU.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why doesn't Yoda have a lightsaber in the original trilogy?
Answer: Because he didn’t need it. Yoda was meant to be the very pinnacle of Force wisdom and power. It wasn’t George’s intention for him to even require a lightsaber to begin with. The same went for Palpatine, who never had a lightsaber during the entire original trilogy. Instead, he opted to use Force attacks. The idea was that both Palpatine and Yoda were people so invested in the Force that they operated in a completely different league, making a lightsaber unnecessary. However, as time progressed and the prequels came about, it seemed overcomplicated and out of place for Yoda to fight with the Force against some of the most powerful Force users. So, they eventually gave both him and Palpatine lightsabers.

Name: Crantzer
Question: All the Jedi are teleported to the Jedi Temple just before Order 66. How long can they hold off Anakin and the Clones?
Answer: Oh, they’d definitely win. Palpatine’s entire plan included that the greatest of Jedi would be away from the Temple during Order 66. Because of this (and with the fact that the attack was unexpected), the Temple was ill-prepared for what was to come. Had this not occurred, it’s unlikely that the 501st and Anakin would’ve been as successful as they were. Think about it: Each Jedi could take on at least a dozen clones. Adding the thousands of Jedi who were overseas would’ve been more than enough to defeat them.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who was the most useless character in Avengers: Endgame?
Answer: Korg. Not only was the big rock man useless in the movie, but he actually made things worse. He was one of Thor’s closest friends and helped feed him into a giant rabbit hole of Cheez-Whiz after what happened in Infinity War. Korg is one of those friends who always follows your lead, and thus never actually gives you the help/motivation you need when you’re in a bad place.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are some kaiju monsters that are underrated?
Answer: Definitely the Kaiju from Invincible. This beast is seriously underrated. Omni-Man has been said to be one of the most powerful Viltrumites in the Empire, and he didn’t stand a damn chance of even running away from the Kaiju in their final fight: Even an attack from both Mark and his dad was difficult. The sheer strength and power of this beast could easily make him one of the most powerful Kaijus to exist in television or movie history.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If the clones did not have inhibitor chips, would they have executed Order 66 or would they refuse and remain loyal to the Jedi?
Answer: No. Clone troopers were imbedded with loyalty and determination. Those who fought side-by-side and served Jedi commanders (which were most clones) would more than likely trust them completely and be on their side, despite what the Senate or Emperor might say. Many examples of this (like Skywalker’s 501st, Plo Koon’s 104th, and Yoda’s 41st) have been shown to grow very fond of their commanding Jedi generals. It’s likely this was the case with most clones under Jedi. That being said, I don’t think Palpatine would have even ordered the manufacturing of the clones if they didn’t have the inhibitor chips to begin with. Clone troopers were the finest of soldiers — they were literally bred for battle. Having them siding with the Jedi would have been too great a risk for Palpatine. So no, Order 66 wouldn’t happen if the clone troopers didn’t have inhibitor chips.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How was Vision able to lift Thor's hammer? Is he worthy?
Answer: Because he’s pure of heart. Vision has absolutely no personal interests, vendettas, or prejudices. He makes it very clear that the only “side” he takes is life itself. There is quite literally no “dirt” you could pull up on Vision. Because of this, he makes for the perfect candidate to be able to life Thor’s hammer.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why isn't Tony Stark blamed for creating Ultron?
Answer: Oh, he definitely was blamed. That being said, it wasn’t all Tony’s fault. For one, Bruce played just as much a part in creating him. Wanda also played a part for instilling that fear-mongering vision inside his head.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What movie villain did you end up admiring or respecting?
Answer: Tai Lung from Kung Fu Panda. Lung was a guy who had his entire childhood ripped from him by Shifu’s overly ambitious plans of making him into a killing machine. He went through decades of blood-inducing training only to be rejected for the one thing he worked toward his entire life — becoming the dragon warrior. In fact, Lung was so well-sympathized by test audiences that the writers decided to add the scene in the movie where he massacred an entire village.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who is the most forgotten/underrated MCU character?
Answer: Definitely Ho Yinsen. Yinsen single-handedly helped Tony escape terrorist captivity and sacrificed his life for him. And mind you, this is the same Yinsen who got ignored by Tony years ago. Almost every line from this man oozes wisdom and selflessness. Even when facing death, all he could think about was seeing his family. He then left some parting words of wisdom that would forever change Tony: The man is the very definition of a legend, and he was the one to finally turn Tony’s life around — he quite literally helped create the Iron Man we all know and love today.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Which Captain America is more powerful, Steve Rogers or John Walker? Why?
Answer: I’m not sure how this isn’t more obvious. Bucky put up a good fight against Cap, putting him around Steve’s level. This same Bucky (with the help of Falcon) struggled much more against John Walker. Whether or not you argue that Bucky was without morals against Cap but not Walker, that doesn’t negate the fact that John’s strength and power is something neither Bucky nor Steve has ever shown. The new super soldier serum (which is the one Walker takes) has already been noted to be stronger than the old one. And by the looks of it, it's by a considerable margin. While you could argue that Steve has more super soldier experience, Walker was still a very skilled soldier who spent years being one of the best fighters in the military, even before he had the serum. He is a formidable foe. Combine this with the fact that he has less morals and more blood lust than Cap, and I’d reckon he beats Steve more often than not.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How did Robert Downey Jr. get so skinny for Avengers: Endgame?
Answer: There was no need for Downey to “slim down” just for the beginning of the movie — and their was a much simpler solution: CGI. Marvel has used special effects to make people much skinnier in the past. Tony’s change was more subtle, so it didn’t require as much. However, special effects were still used.
