Name: Crantzer
Question: If Iron Man 2 had taken place in the real world, how would the Senate hearing with Tony Stark have ended? Would the US government have succeeded in taking the Iron Man suit away from Stark?
Answer: Honestly, no. Lawmakers know what they’re doing. While there may be a long and painful process to try to get Tony’s property, they eventually wouldn’t for the sole fact that they can’t. The government knows they won’t get their hands on Tony’s tech either way. But at the point of Iron Man 2, Tony had been aligned with America’s interest. Thus, it’s unlikely that they would push him so far as to make him a fugitive of the country. He was valuable to them. As long as he serves their interest, Tony should be fine.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How much did Robert Downey, Jr. make in Iron Man 1 and 2?
Answer: He didn’t make much at first. Iron Man was a risky movie John Favreau directed because there was absolutely no way to know if it’d be successful. For all they knew, it was going to be a flop. Because of this, Downey initially made a measly $500,000 on his first Iron Man movie[1]. However, after the booming success of the MCU, Downey received another $50 million for the first movie. Every other Iron Man role Downey made in the MCU after was a much nicer paycheck. Still during its beginnings in the MCU (yet a few years after Iron Man), Robert’s $500,000 paycheck turned into $10 million[2] for being in Iron Man 2.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In MCU Iron Man, why hasn't the US government replicated Tony Stark's suit when they essentially have access to his technology, the War Machine?
Answer: The same reason we can’t replicate it today: The arc reactor. Every other part of the Iron Man suit is more than possible to build (the outer suit, the exoskeleton, the HUD smart display, the weaponry, and the jetpacks). In fact, most of these components are already developed in Iron Man suits today. However, the arc reactor is far beyond our time. This hockey-sized portable energy source houses the power of around eight nuclear reactors. There’s just no way to create something like that with today’s technology. The government in Iron Man 2 ran into this same problem — so instead of building their own suit, they improved on Tony’s.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why does Loki keep betraying Thor?
Answer: Greed and jealousy. Ever since they were children, both Thor and Loki were raised under the assumption that they were rulers of the realms — powerful beings far beyond mortal men. But of course, the throne could only be given to one. This intrinsic idea of ruling being their nature was what prompted Loki to seek power so desperately. He makes it very clear he believed it was his right: Loki: “I went down to Midgard to rule the people of Earth as a benevolent god, just like you.” Odin: “…all because Loki desires a throne.” Loki: “It is my birthright!” That was why Loki constantly betrayed Thor: because his brother was the only thing standing in his way to what he believed he deserved — a throne.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did Iron Man deserve to die?
Answer: He didn’t deserve to, but he was destined to. Out of the millions of possibilities Strange saw, there was only one in which they won — Tony had to sacrifice himself. It was meant to happen.

Name: Crantzer
Question: You're an employee/employer at Wayne Enterprises, and you suspect your boss (Bruce Wayne) is Batman. What do you do?
Answer: This situation actually happened in The Dark Knight. A Wayne Enterprises employee found out about Bruce’s gadgets and came to the understanding that he was Batman. He then attempted to blackmail him with this information. Lucius Fox then shut the idiot down very gracefully: So no, I wouldn’t do a damn thing if I found out Bruce Wayne was Batman.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How much would a real Iron Man suit cost?
Answer: So, here’s the thing: Almost every aspect of the Iron Man suit (from its exoskeleton, jetpacks, VR display, weaponry, and neuro-link) is possible to build today, and altogether cost a few dozen million dollars. For most big-name companies, that’s very affordable, and it’s even why some Iron Man suits exist today. However, there is one part of the suit that is impossible to re-create: the arc reactor. The arc reactor is a portable energy source the size of a hockey puck, powering the equivalent of around eight nuclear power plants. There is just no technology in our time to even come close to that. If such a power source were to be developed today, it would likely turn those millions of dollars of a suit expense into tens of billions just for the power source alone.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who was missing from Tony Stark's funeral?
Answer: While it is true that people like Gamora and Valkyrie missed his funeral, there is another important one a lot of people fail to mention: Phil Coulson. While it is true that Loki killed him in The Avengers, SHIELD actually revived Coulson with Kree blood in Agents of SHIELD. Thus, it would’ve been nice for him to surprise everyone with an appearance. Phil was one of the key people to bring the Avengers together. They all mourned his death and were close to him. It seems fitting for him to have been at Tony’s.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What can Captain America do without his shield? Why is he even considered a superhero?
Answer: Cap is exponentially more than just his shield. He managed to: Stop a helicopter with his hands, Hold off Thanos with five Infinity Stones, Take out nine high-class government agents in combat, Go toe-to-toe with Bucky after he stole his shield, Outclass Batroc, And defeat an entire boat of enemies.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why was Padmé made to still appear pregnant for her funeral?
Answer: Because Luke and Leia’s birth was never made public. No one knew of Anakin and Padme’s relationship — it was always a secret. Hearing that their kids were alive would stir great drama. But more importantly, had Palpatine (or especially Vader) received word that not just one but two of the Chosen One’s kids were alive, they would stop at nothing to find them and make them tools for the Empire.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are some really cool, easily missed details that movies have in them?
Answer: An increase in corporate power throughout time. This is Buy n Large. Most casual Pixar viewers know it as the corporation that runs everything in Wall-E. However, Buy n Large actually exists in numerous Pixar films, and we see its progression in power over time. In Toy Story 3, you see their logo on Buzz’s batteries. By the time you get to the movie Up, BNL is involved in the construction business, and they’re even buying out all the houses in the area. Later on, we see BNL’s logo appear in the stadium in Cars 3. Finally, we see in Wall-E that the company runs pretty much everything and that its CEO is essentially a world leader. The world is basically run under the control of BNL.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is a small detail from a movie that stands out to you?
Answer: When J Jonah Jameson gets interrogated by Green Goblin in Spider-Man. Notice what he says: It’s honestly an incredible line that I brushed off as a kid. Despite how he may act around his employees, Jameson is still loyal to the end. He had absolutely no reason to protect Peter’s identity, but he did. He might be hard-headed, but he sure as hell is just as much a man of integrity and loyalty. This is also why Jameson was so angry about writing a retraction. He didn’t have to, but in the name of good journalism and transparency, James decided it was the right thing to do — even if that meant apologizing to the masked vigilante he hates so much.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How would I make an Iron Man suit?
Answer: Funnily enough, it’s mostly possible. Former Mythbusters star Adam Savage built the world’s first flying Iron Man suit. It was a fully functioning body suit with flight capability. Nearly every single part of the Iron Man suit already exists in some form - an exoskeleton, bulletproof armor, and HUD Display. However, there is one aspect of the suit that just isn’t possible to replicate: its compact energy source. The sheer amount of energy that Tony’s arc reactor outputs is far higher than any portable energy the world can come up with. He quite literally has the power of a nuclear plant inside a small reactor. Nothing close to that is available or foreseeable in our world anytime soon. Because of this one obstacle, it’s likely that we’ll never truly get a completely accurate Iron Man that lasts more than 10 minutes on power.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How did non-Clone Navy officers react to Order 66?
Answer: While it is true that most Officers were indifferent to Order 66, there was one who actually sided with the Jedi: Commander Teron. Teron saw the honorable actions of the Jedi firsthand during the Clone Wars. He understood that they would never betray the Republic and that it was instead the Jedi who were betrayed. After the Empire rose to power, Teron came to discover the existence of surviving Jedi Master K’Kruhk, along with a few other younglings. Teron then called K’Kruhk to speak to him privately. At first, K’Kruhk confronted him on Order 66 and why he betrayed the Jedi, but the Commander explained that he was only aware of it when it was too late. Teron admitted to becoming hopeful after learning that K’Kruhk had a group of younglings with him, understanding that the future of the Jedi had not fully been erased. Teron then came to aid K’Kruhk and the others by providing them goods with his own salary, as well as making sure that no Imperial eyes came near their hideout.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why Iron Man is called Iron Man when there is no iron in his armor?
Answer: Tony actually addressed this the first time he heard the name Iron Man: "Iron Man. That’s kind of catchy, it’s got a nice ring to it. I mean, it’s not technically accurate - the suit’s a gold titanium alloy, but it’s kind of provocative; the imagery, anyway." The point of the name was not to be accurate to the material of the suit - it was trying to be catchy and iconic. The same goes for Black Widow, Batman, Superman, and Wonder Woman…they make no sense, but they’re iconic as hell.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is the reason for Yoda's strange behavior in Return of the Jedi?
Answer: Yoda was trying to test Luke’s patience. Yoda was very aware of Luke was, and he knew of the boy’s potential. He had to be sure, before training him, that he possessed the patience and discipline of a true Jedi. That being said, Yoda is of course also a goofball.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If “I am Groot” is a language and not a name, what is Groot’s real name?
Answer: It’s not what you think. Remember how Thor says he learned Groot? Now notice how Thor introduces Groot to Steve: Is it possible that Groot’s real name is Tree?!

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Black Panther call Bucky the “White Wolf” in Avengers: Infinity War?
Answer: It was a reference to the comics. In comics, the White Wolf is a completely different person. His name is Hunter. He and his family had crash-landed in Wakanda, so King T’Chaka decided to adopt and train him. Thus, Hunter is T’Challa’s brother. Hunter eventually became a warrior (like the Black Panther), completely loyal to Wakanda. The MCU likes to change up things from comics or cartoons, so it’s likely that Bucky is just their version of the White Wolf. And with this, it’s plausible that we’ll see this mantle of White Wolf used in the future for Bucky to serve the people of Wakanda in their time of need, for everything they’d done for him.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who will become the new Iron Man type character after Endgame?
Answer: There are multiple options Marvel has: It’s possible that Morgan Stark might take the mantle of Iron Man, seeing as she is Tony’s daughter after all. It also looks like the MCU tried to make Riri Williams (aka Ironheart) the next Iron Man figure, but it’s unlikely she’ll make a major return anytime soon after the intense criticism of her character. However, there’s also another option: given the widespread introduction to the multiverse, it’s entirely possible that we may get to see alternate dimensions of Tony Stark.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why isn't Tony Stark hiding his identity as Iron Man?
Answer: While it is true Tony being capable of defending himself and being already accustomed to fame are big reasons why he revealed himself as Iron Man, there is one other major reason that many people miss. Notice what he says to the public right after his captivity: Tony was tired of not taking responsibility for his actions. He decided to openly accept that whatever Iron Man did, he did. He didn’t want to cower behind a helmet and not take responsibility for the damage he would cause. And as to the second point, Tony made do on his promise that he has “more to offer this world than just making things that blow up” - he made a suit of armor around the world that led to unprecedented world peace.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Tony Stark (Iron Man) smarter than Bruce Wayne, given that most of Batman's tech is developed for him?
Answer: Yes. First, I want to get one thing out of the way: Batman is way smarter than you seem to give him credit for. He built the entire Batcave all by himself, He built a Kryptonite suit to take on the most powerful man in the world, He studied & mastered 127 styles of martial arts, And he has twelve Masters degrees in various fields. That being said, Bruce’s intellect is far behind Tony’s. Since his childhood, Stark was the very pinnacle of intelligence. As a kid, he built robots and AI for fun (and even hacked the Pentagon on a dare), He’s impossibly quick to learn, And he made a suit of armor decades ahead of its time with a box of scraps. But of course, his most impressive display of intelligence was the Iron Man suits, which got even more advanced as time progressed. The most advanced suit was so powerful that it matched blow-for-blow with the Mad Titan himself (a man feared across the entire universe), and it even withstood an Infinity Stone! That’s not to mention its self-healing properties. Bruce is likely more tactful than Tony in the sense that he has better quick thinking in high-stakes situations. However, there is no question that Tony is far smarter than Batman. Tony’s greatest creation looked like literal magic. As smart as Batman is, he’s never come close to that.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is there any water on Coruscant?
Answer: Yes. There was only one visible body of water on Coruscant - the Great Western Sea. Oddly enough, Vader actually owned a property right next to the sea, which acted as a beach resort. And while it is unknown whether or not Vader actually used it, it is an interesting thought.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did Tony Stark know that Captain America knew his dad?
Answer: Oh, yes. Back in The Avengers, Tony mentioned that his dad always talked about Steve: He said this again in Civil War:

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is the most powerful moment in the Marvel Cinematic Universe?
Answer: I’d have to say this scene from The Winter Soldier: This was the ultimate sacrifice play. Cap was willing to sacrifice his life rather than kill his friend. He deeply cared about Buck, and he knew that even if death was what would come, it was worth taking it. That’s the definition of friendship. That’s what loyalty looks like.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What movie could have been over in 10 minutes if the main character wasn't such a fool?
Answer: Revenge of the Sith. Had Anakin had an ounce of sense in him, he’d have taken Dooku in for questioning instead of just killing him on the spot for no good reason. He was a valuable asset. Of course, that’s not to mention that had Anakin waited just ten more seconds, Dooku definitely would’ve ratted Palpatine out after he betrayed him.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why doesn't anyone recognize Superman?
Answer: People aren’t as observant as you think. Superman actor Henry Cavill actually tested this idea in Times Square during the Dawn of Justice premiere. Cavill stood in front of his movie poster in the middle of Times Square, with a Superman shirt on. And funnily enough, not one person recognized him. The world is a pretty big place. We hardly ever look at some random person long enough to think, “That might be a secretly famous person without glasses!”.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are the most ridiculous things about Avengers: Infinity War?
Answer: Probably when Gamora decided to go to Knowhere. Gamora was the only one to know about where the Soul Stone was. She knew damn well that she was the Mad Titan’s prime target (which is why she told Quill to kill her in the event that she gets caught). But, instead of going to Nivadellir with Thor (or anywhere else, for that matter), she decided to go right to where Thanos was in order to “prevent him from getting the reality stone”. This turned out to be a huge mistake, because wouldn’t you know it, Thanos did end up capturing her.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Which MCU scene do you dislike the most? Why?
Answer: Definitely this idiotic line from The Falcon & The Winter Soldier: In case you’re not aware, he’s referring to the Flag Smashers (whose leader was Karli Morgenthau). This is the same organization who: Robbed a bank, Beat the living daylights out of both Bucky and Sam, Bombed a supply depot with dozens of civilians, And threatened Sam’s sister’s family. The entire speech Sam gave in the finale was completely moronic, and it tried to give sympathy to a literal terrorist organization. Think about it: they were a group of people who used unlawful violence in pursuit of political aims. That is the very definition of a terrorist! In all honesty, it felt like Sam was trying really hard to make that speech Cap gave back in The Winter Soldier. Sam’s speech was…let’s just say a much worse version.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In Star Wars, who’s the most underrated Jedi?
Answer: Definitely Ezra Bridger. Ezra is far more powerful than most people think. He only had around 3–4 years of training under Kanan, and during that period he very quickly gained immense power. In fact, his lightsaber skill became so enhanced that it exceeded that of his master Kanan, a guy who trained in the Jedi Order. But perhaps Ezra’s most notable change was in the Force. For example, he was able to master the very rare ability of mind control. The most advanced of his Force power, however, was his ability to talk to animals. He was able to communicate with Force wolves, and most impressively even controlled purrgil’s — interdimensional space whales who traveled at light speed. Ezra is criminally underrated in terms of power. With due training, he could very well be one of the most powerful Jedi of his time, maybe even surpassing Ahsoka.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why does Kylo Ren have black hair?
Answer: Haha, well the same can be asked about Luke’s hair. The answer might just be in the fact that both parents having one hair color doesn’t mean that the child has to. Black hair is a dominant gene, so it’s likely it passed through either Padme or Anakin’s side, and then just hit Kylo right in the head. Of course, I wouldn’t put it past Kylo to just dye it for the emo effect. He was quite dramatic, after all.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If Ego from Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 were a good guy, could he have stopped Thanos from ever succeeding in his plan?
Answer: Absolutely. Ego was a man of unparalleled power - by all accounts, he was a Celestial. He was also virtually indestructible (the exception being through his brain). Had Thanos attacked any part of his body, he could simply regenerate it. Thanos was no match for him. Being the intelligent man he was, Thnos likely knew this. This is why I firmly believe that Thanos waited as long as he did to get the stones - in order to allow the most powerful of the universe to die out so he could strike at the right time.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Ego admit to Star Lord that he put the tumor into his mother’s head?
Answer: Because he had no humanity. Ego was a being of unparalleled age and power. Most (if not, all) mortal beings were far beneath him in his eyes, so he became desensitized to the concept of killing and destroying. It became, like all sociopaths, natural to him. It’s highly likely that Ego, during his long life, has seen countless deaths and destruction. Killing a woman he knew for mere moments (relative to his age) would be insignificant to him. Essentially, Ego didn’t understand that it wasn’t appropriate to say. He didn’t think it would bother Quill all that much, seeing as he was an “eternal being” like him. Surely, the deaths of mortals were beneath Quill. But he turned out to be very wrong.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What MCU scenes would lead to a public backlash if the gender roles were reversed?
Answer: Definitely this scene from Captain America: The First Avenger: Private Lorraine took a keen interest in Steve and started heavily flirting with him. Steve was into Peggy at the time, so he had no interest in Lorraine and thus got physically uncomfortable. However, she didn’t take the hint and decided to pull him aside and kiss him without consent. Steve was flustered so he didn’t refuse, but this was far from a mutual kiss. It also led to tension between Peggy and Steve later on. If the roles were reversed, someone would definitely get reprimanded (or worse) by HR.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In his last years, did Maul know that Vader was Anakin Skywalker?
Answer: Oh, yes. Before anyone else, Maul knew what Anakin would become. He saw the visions of what would happen and knew he had to try to stop it. That’s why he orchestrated the entire Mandalore War - to lure Skywalker so he could kill him. That being said, there’s no guarantee that Maul would manage to kill Anakin, even if his plan to lure him to Mandalore was successful.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In Avengers: Infinity War, Thor takes the power of a star. Could any other Avengers survive this?
Answer: While it is true that people like Captain Marvel and Hulk might be able to survive this, there is one who many people fail to mention: Dr. Strange. “What an idiotic opinion. Strange is just a human, he couldn’t be able to take a fraction of that power!” Well, actually he can - but only with prep. Back in What If, we’re introduced to a very interesting spell. This spell was a durability spell that would be able to protect the user from immensely powerful attacks. Even Strange Supreme had trouble destroying it. Strange Supreme’s blasts have been seen to wreck entire reality. And yet, even that wasn’t enough to destroy the Guardian Vishanti spell. I’m pretty sure a dying neutron star would be fine.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why was almost everyone able to lift Thor's hammer in "Thor: Love and Thunder"?
Answer: I assume you’re referring to Stormbreaker (seeing as Mjolnir was only ever weilded by Jane and Thor in the movie). The answer is actually very simple and something way too many people fail to understand: You don’t need to be worthy to lift Stormbreaker! Unlike Mjolinr, Stormbreaker was never enchanted to only be held by those who were “worthy”. It was simply a powerfully-forged weapon with near-indestructible properties. We see many people lift Stormbreaker, including Groot and Thanos. You’d be surprised how many people forget this fact.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In the movie Ragnarok, how did Odin's power compare to Surtur's?
Answer: Well, as the story goes, Odin actually defeated Surtur in his most powerful form. Mind you, this is the same Surtur who destroyed Hela effortlessly, incinerated Asgard in minutes, and swatted the Hulk like a fly. And that same Hela was the one who easily beat Thor in his awakened state, soloed the entire Asgardian army, and even brushed past an Infinity Stone. It goes to show just how powerful Odin in his prime truly was.

Name: Crantzer
Question: When Captain America said “Avengers Assemble”, how did the Avengers at the very back hear him? Captain America said it very softly.
Answer: They didn’t. Right after Cap said “assemble”, Thor made a very loud war cry. This was what then prompted T’Challa’s war cry and attack with his army. This domino effect was what eventually led everyone else to attack. This is how it works in real war as well. One guy doesn’t just yell “Attack”, the divided sections of the army will attack when they see others doing it.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is something you noticed in Avengers: Infinity War that you believe others have missed?
Answer: Remember this scene at the beginning of the film of Tony contemplating whether or not to call Cap? Notice the number on the phone: See how the fourth digit is 1? According to the North American Numbering Plan, it is impossible to have a phone number that starts with 1 after the area code. This is why every single phone number we see in the MCU actually starts with 1. So unfortunately, you will be unable to get an answer if you try to call Steve Rogers.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is something you noticed in Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015) that you believe others have missed?
Answer: At the end of the movie, Lara Barton (Hawkeye’s wife) sends a video message to Natasha. The video message is of Clint and Lara’s son Nathaniel. Notice the middle name? They named him Pietro. This was done in honor of Wanda’s brother Pietro, who saved Clint’s life by sacrificing his own.

Name: Crantzer
Question: When someone has the Infinity Gauntlet, do you choose who gets dusted, because when Tony snapped his fingers, none of the Avengers got dusted?
Answer: Yes. The Infinity Gauntlet had unparalleled levels of power. The wielder, if strong enough, could easily wipe out the universe if they wanted to. We actually see Infinity Ultron do this in What If, and Thanos even said he would do that in Endgame: Thanos had the power to destroy the universe. Instead, he made the choice in Infinity War to dust away a random half of the population. That means you can control who is affected by the snap. That being said, I don’t think the snap can actually dust away the entire universe’s population. Why do I say this? Well, take a look back to when Infinity Ultron had the stones. He actually wanted to destroy the entire universe. If he could’ve just snapped to get rid of everyone, then why would he go out of his way to form an army and attack everywhere?

Name: Crantzer
Question: Could Ironman beat Superman?
Answer: It’s commonly understood that Iron Man traditionally stands no chance against the Man of Steel. However, there is one version of Iron Man that would completely demolish Supes - The Godkiller Armor Mark II. This absolute behemoth of a weapon is powered by eight nuclear reactors. It was built to defeat Dark Celestials, which were ancient beings of unparalleled, universal power (far more powerful than Superman has ever been). As for speed, the armor’s flight capabilities were so advanced that it traveled from Mars to Earth in a matter of minutes. It was only through the attack by numerous Celestials from all fronts that the armor eventually got to critical condition. This version of Iron Man could absolutely demolish the Son of Krypton - easily, I might add. That being said, most other versions of Tony’s armor wouldn’t see the light of day in a fight against Superman.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Which actor has played the best Superman?
Answer: This one’s an unpopular opinion, but… Personally, my absolute favorite Superman actor has to go to Tyler Hoechlin from Superman & Lois. Hoechlin’s performance as Clark Kent is absolutely phenomenal, and I believe he’s gotta be the closest to the comic book adaption as we’ve ever got. You see, Hoechlin’s Superman has something no other has: A family. Clark is a family man who, in the show, goes out of his way to balance both protecting the planet and his family. It portrays Clark in a new light of prioritizing his kids and family, showing just how much more difficult it is to juggle both a family and world-saving. There’s something “classic-feeling” about his character that makes him stand out amongst the others. EDIT: Just in case you wanted a little preview of how Clark is in the show, here’s a scene where he confronts a guy who threatened his family:

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is the saddest line in a Marvel movie?
Answer: Probably this heartbreaking scene from The Winter Soldier: This scene really broke me. Steve had sacrificed everything for the world, and he came back after decades to see Peggy again. But all he realizes, even after his insightful conversation with her, is that she’s never going to be the same way she was. She’s different now, and it’s time for him to move on as well. Everyone who’s ever lost the love of their life knows that pain. However, this line also has a much deeper meaning. Notice what Peggy told him: “All we can do is our best. And sometimes the best that we can do is to start over.” Cap took that lesson to heart. What did he do after realizing the best thing for him to do? He started over.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is the most underrated weapon in the MCU?
Answer: Hela’s Necroswords. You know…the ones that somehow come out of her body. These were the same bad boys that eradicated the entire Valkyrie (an elite fighting force in the most powerful kingdom of the nine realms) with ease. Of course, Hela then used it to incinerate the entire Asgardian army. But probably the most impressive thing Hela’s done with the Necroswords that most people don’t consider is that it can cut through Uru, just like it did against Skurge’s Uru armor.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why are so many movies trying to humanize villains and make them more relatable?
Answer: Because it makes for a more elaborate film. Take, for example, Thanos. In comics, Thanos went to snap half of all life away just to impress the goddess of death (a woman he had a major crush on). But instead of this approach, the MCU’s Russo brothers decided to make him a more understanding person who believed it was his destiny to erase half of all life in order to provide more resources to the other half, making them “thrive”. This change didn’t make Thanos a more “relatable” character per se, but it did make him more understandable and humanized. Instead of a one-dimensional monster who was the doom of the universe, the Mad Titan instead became a man who felt burdened by destiny and scarred by the trauma of his home world. In the end, this change led (at least in my view and most others) to a more enjoyable watch for both Infinity War and Endgame - because a villain who is more fleshed out and understandable is usually a better villain.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are the most accurate comic book live action castings ever?
Answer: While there are good answers here like J. Jonah Jameson, Red Skull, and Joker, there is one that I’m surprised no one has mentioned: Dr. Strange. Pretty much everything about Strange (from his outfit to his spells to his character) is almost completely spot-on. It really resembles the idea of a severely powerful being putting together the multiverse the best he can. His character, like the comics, is also deeply similar in the sense that they were both formerly-egotistical individuals who gained a fresh understanding of humility through the lens of their minuscule part to play in the grand multiverse. That’s all not to mention that Benedict Cumberbatch nailed the hell out of the role.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Was Thor right when he blamed Loki for Odin’s death?
Answer: Absolutely. “But Loki put Odin in a nursing home! Whatever happened after wasn’t his fault!” Doesn’t matter. Loki not only put Odin in a place he’d rarely been, but he also cast a spell making him unable to even think properly. Everything about the spell he cast and the place he put him in made the All-Father in danger. And if he did truly care about him, then he would’ve at the very least checked in on him every once and a while. But clearly, he didn’t. But another thing a lot of people fail to mention is that the very spell Loki put on Odin was what led him to die in the first place! Upon being put in this spell, Odin’s powers had been slowly draining for years. It was up until the point that Loki and Thor came to see their father that Odin eventually couldn’t last any longer and turned into pure force (the Odinforce).

Name: Crantzer
Question: Does Earth exist in the Star Wars universe?
Answer: In Legends, yes. In Disney’s Star Tours, we see that Earth is one of several regular intergalactic trade routes with other planets like Kashyyk, Tatooine, and even the first Death Star. The year this takes place is 2500 AD. There’s also a Legends comic called Into the Great Unknown, where both Han and Chewbacca head to a hostile and indigenous planet. Eventually, Han dies a gruesome death by an arrow and Chewie is stranded. The remains of Solo’s body are found by none other than Indiana Jones. This confirms that the planet in which this took place was Earth.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why didn't Tony Stark wish that he wouldn't die from using the Infinity Gauntlet as his first wish?
Answer: Because the Gauntlet wasn’t a genie. You don’t just “make a wish” and expect the Gauntlet to do the rest — despite its power, it still had constraints. While you could accomplish a lot of what you might wish for, it doesn’t just accomplish anything, it has to stay within the realms of science and fate. For example, the Gauntlet cannot bring back people from the dead. Hulk already tried that with Natasha. The power of the Infinity Stones are, according to Ronan, unable to be wielded mortals without dying. And that statement sounds entirely accurate, seeing that even a beast like Hulk got injured from it. Despite his intellect and gadgets, Tony was still a simple man. He had no powers. He knew he’d die doing what was right, but he was willing to make the sacrifice play. That’s what makes him the most powerful Avenger.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why didn't Hulk use the infinity gauntlet again to save Tony Stark aka Iron Man?
Answer: Remember what Banner said about Nat? Hulk already tried to bring one dead person back to life. Tony would be no different. You see, the stones didn’t bring back people who died naturally — that was their fate. All it did was bring those who were affected by the snap. That’s it. Besides, Tony’s sacrifice was great enough to earn the respect of the entire universe. Bringing him back after all that would have done nothing but cheapen the gesture.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Didn't Avengers: Endgame prove that Tony Stark was right in Captain America: Civil War, as Thanos's snap in Avengers: Infinity War was literally what he was trying to avoid?
Answer: No. It seems you miss the entire point about Civil War. It wasn’t in order to “prevent future calamity”, it was a question of whether or not there should be government oversight. Cap believed that the safest hands were still their own, while Tony believed that they needed someone to keep them responsible. But more so than that, there was a whole other layer to the whole dilemma: Cap was trying to protect his friend. All Steve was really trying to do was protect Bucky and keep him safe. It’s why he went after to find him and went with him to track down Zemo (in order to protect Buck for the future). But more so than the government disagreement, the whole thing with Tony finding out Bucky killed his parents was what set him over the edge. And it’s also what led to their very intense fight (seeing as Cap was trying to protect Bucky from getting killed). Think about it this way: Whether or not Tony sided with Steve or vice-versa, they would still have had unity. And with that unification, they’d likely be at least considerably more formidable against Thanos than they were. That’s why Tony blamed Steve in Endgame - because he blamed him for “breaking them up” (seeing as Cap was the one who was a fugitive). But in reality, Steve could make the exact same argument. Whatever the reason and whoever was right, the point remains that the very fact that they broke up was the reason Thanos was so successful in getting the stones. In conclusion, no. Endgame doesn’t prove Tony was “right” about the Accords because:

Name: Crantzer
Question: Will Tony Stark be alive?
Answer: It’s possible. In comics, Tony actually uploaded his consciousness into an AI making him “alive”, but he pretended to be a simple program for a while in order to not give the notion that he actually was still alive. We see something similar in the MCU. While it is said to only be a recording that he made in the past, it seems that there is a digital “message” that Tony leaves to those when he died, just like in comics. But what makes this interesting is that right at the end of his message, Tony actually made eye contact with his daughter while saying “I love you 3000”. Does this mean that, just like in comics, Tony does have a living being uploaded somewhere? Maybe. But Robert Downey Jr. has been pretty adamant about not coming back in the MCU. That being said, Disney will go to great lengths if a cameo makes them money. A cameo of some kind from Iron Man is never out of the question.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if Anakin and Padme raised Luke and Leia?
Answer: There are two ways this could go down: The first way is that Padme joined Anakin in his plans to rule the Empire after killing Palpatine. This would then allow him to raise his family alongside his family, which was what he wanted in the first place. Together, they’d be unstoppable. The second way is if Anakin never fell. This one’s the closest to reality. Had Anakin never bought Palpatine’s lies and killed/arrested him the moment he admitted to being the Sith Lord, Anakin would’ve prevented Palpatine from executing Order 66 and subsequently taking control of the Empire. Seeing the sheer power Anakin had (and thus the potential of his children), it’s likely they’d be trained in the Jedi Temple and live amongst those that Anakin cared about all his life, including Kenobi and Ahsoka.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Who has the strongest will in the MCU?
Answer: While there are some great answers here (like Cap and Tony), there is one who’s will is severely underrated: Doctor Strange. A lot of people tend to forget the sheer impact and sacrifice Strange made back against Dormammu: Even with all the power he accumulated, Strange didn’t stand a chance against the beast that was Dormammu. And yet, he didn’t let that stop him, so he decided to allow himself to suffer for eternity to save humanity. He’d die again and again (and even felt the pain each and every time), but he decided to continue so that the people on earth could live. It’s honestly the greatest show of sacrifice and will in the entire MCU.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Revelation 9:18 about people who preach hell?
Answer: No. It’s important not to just look at one verse, but at the full context. Revelation Chapter 9 is a continuation of the seven trumpet judgments that the Lord is putting against those who take the mark of the beast and worship his name. Prior to this, there has been a massive amount of persecution against Jews and Christians, and thus the Lord decides the time has come for judgment for the people who continue to rebel against Him. The verse in question, Revelation 9:18, is referring to the sixth trumpet, and it says this: “By these three plagues a third of mankind was killed—by fire and the smoke and the brimstone which came out of their mouths” (Rev. 9:18, NKJV). Due to the severity of humanity’s apostasy at the time, one of the trumpet judgments that the Lord will inflict upon the rebels in the world is that he will cause plagues to kill a third of mankind. In conclusion, Revelation 9:18 does not describe those who preach hell (which is a very real truth to preach about), but it instead describes those who rebel against the Lord and side with the antichrist in the last days.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why does Darkseid always have his hands behind his back?
Answer: Simple — to insight fear. Observe his stance: Most notably and importantly, the hands behind the back is a display of power. He’s showing that he’s not too concerned with whatever feeble attempt one may have against him, and he shows as much by showing that he doesn’t even need his hands to beat you. The hands behind his back with the back posture also makes the guy look as big and intimidating as possible. He’s also spread his feet a bit in order to assert a level of dominance.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What would happen if Palpatine accidentally said "Order 65" instead of Order 66?
Answer: Palpatine: “Commander Cody, execute Order 65…wait, I mea-”. Commander Cody: “It will be done, my lord.” Palpatine: “No, wai-” *comms turn off* Palpatine: “Ah, dank farrik...” Order 65 was a contingency plan that stated that if a majority of the Senate declared that the Chancellor was unfit for duty, he/she were to be arrested, or killed if necessary. Because of this, Palpatine would have been put in custody until all of his schemes had been sorted out, and he’d have been caught before he could destroy the Republic. “This was not on my vision board…”

Name: Crantzer
Question: If Odin built Asgard, what was there before Asgard?
Answer: He didn’t. Odin’s father Bor has the title of “Architect of Asgard”. He built the foundations of the great empire that it became, and it was thanks to him that Asgard became as prosperous as it was. So then, what existed before Asgard? Well, numerous other realms existed long before Asgard ever did. In comics, Bor seems to have originated either from Niflheim or the space between Niflheim and Muspelheim (depending on the source). This means that from either one of these realms came the ancestors that would eventually become Asgard.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are the few rules of chess which are not commonly known?
Answer: There are a few mind-blowing rules that even high-level chess players often don’t know about: After multiple studies, Methylphenidate (most commonly marketed as Ridalin and Modafinil) has been confirmed to increase player performance by an average of 13–15%. Thus, FIDE has banned these drugs at all official tournaments[1] . The rules of the European Chess Union[2] state that female players must wear skirts no shorter than 4 inches above the knee. There is also a rule that only the first and second buttons on a blouse may be opened in order to hide cleavage. This one might be a new one for beginners. While it is true that many casual players say “check” during a game, it is looked down upon and very bad manners to say it in an official tournament. In fact, talking of any kind (unless necessary to the game, like calling an arbiter) during a game is banned[3] .

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why was Loki the only one not surprised when Thor hit Hulk with a hammer and slid across the wall in Thor: Ragnarok?
Answer: Loki was well aware of what Thor was capable of. The people of Sakaar saw Thor as they saw everyone else who fought in the fighting pits - barely competent foes who would die easily at the hands of the green monster. As far as they were concerned, Thor was a dead man. Loki, however, knew Thor for thousands of years - he knew of Thor’s true power. Because of this, it was not at all shocking to him to see the Hulk get thrown across the wall. It comes down to perspective - the people of Sakaar didn’t know Thor’s true power. Loki did.

Name: Crantzer
Question: (Endgame Spoiler) What were Tony's last words?
Answer: Tony’s last words were to the woman who was with him along the entire ride.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What in your opinion is the most realistic scene/moment/line in a comic book movie?
Answer: Definitely this scene from Age of Ultron: This was one of my favorite scenes in a Marvel movie. No supervillains, no crazy feats…just a bunch of people acting like regular buddies, cracking jokes, and talking about their lives. That is something Marvel does best: realism.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Odin strip all power from Thor, but not Loki?
Answer: Because he couldn’t. Thor is an Asgardian god, so his powers come from his bloodline. They came from the very DNA that Odin and his forefathers swore by. That’s why it could be controlled. Loki was different. Unlike his brother, he didn't have any trace of Asgardian DNA in him. His powers were of his frost giant forefathers, which included superhuman strength and durability, amongst other things. But the greatest source of his strength came from the sorcery he learned primarily from his mother. These “witch-like” powers didn’t originate from Asgard, either. So no, Odin couldn’t simply strip Loki of his powers, because the powers were not given to him by Asgardian ancestry.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Would Loki have made a better King than Thor, if Odin had somehow chosen him to be his heir to begin with?
Answer: Oh, no. We don’t need to imagine what Loki would’ve been like as king of Asgard - he already was! Remember this scene? For years, Loki ruled Asgard under Odin’s identity (by transforming himself into his likeness) after banishing his father to Earth, all the way back in The Dark World up until Ragnarok. So, how did Loki do during his time in office? Well, Thor puts it well: Thor: I decided to go out and investigate. And what do I find? The nine realms completely in chaos - enemies around us assembling, plotting our demise all while you, Odin, protector of those nine realms sitting here in your bathrobe eating grapes. Loki: Yes, well it is best to respect our neighbor’s freedoms. Thor: Yes, of course…the freedom to be massacred. Unsurprisingly, Loki didn’t care too much for the real problems across the nine realms - he barely cared about his own people. He simply did what he always enjoyed doing - indulging himself in glory and enjoyment. Loki never gave a damn about the people. He always sought his own self-interests. Being king didn’t change that.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if Odin didn't go to Jotunheim to get Thor and the others?
Answer: Jotunheim would’ve been wiped out. Odin didn’t get involved to save Thor’s life - he went to stop him from slaughtering them. Thor had made it very clear that he was able to kill them all if he wished: The whole purpose of stopping Thor wasn’t to save his life, it was to prevent countless casualties and an escalation of war.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Would you rather have Darth Vader or Lord Voldemort as your father? Why?
Answer: That’s easy. Voldemort only ever sought personal glory. Vader wanted no such thing. Contrary to popular belief, Vader was actually a caring dad. He loved his children, and since the day he realized he had a son, he made it his life’s mission to have him, even if it meant burning down the entire Empire. In his own sick and twisted way, Vader deeply loved his children. It was his one redeeming quality - his love for family. Prior to Padme’s death, it was Vader’s goal to rule the Empire with his family. And even decades later, that dream never ceased.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why exactly is MCU Quill intimidated by Thor? He’s never seen him fight.
Answer: He didn’t need to. This is what Peter eventually found plopped on his ship: Fighting ability aside, the dude’s jacked and very easy on the eyes. Just by looks alone, Peter stands no chance. This was abundantly clear to Peter from the start, and his friends didn’t try to pretend otherwise: Thor became the most intimidating man to Star-Lord without ever having to say a word.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Did Obi-Wan Kenobi live a good life?
Answer: Uh, no. As a kid, Kenobi did so badly in training that the Council thought about making him a farmer. However, eventually, Qui-Gon decided to train him when no one else wanted to. As a Knight, Obi-Wan watched his Master die. As a lover, Obi-Wan watched helplessly as a lightsaber cut through the woman he loved. As a Master, Kenobi watched everything he had lived for crumbling around him. As an old man, he then went into hiding for decades in a hot, deserted wasteland of a planet. Obi-Wan is arguably the greatest tragedy in the entire Star Wars universe. If anyone had reason to fall to the dark side, it was him. A lot more than just losing the woman you impregnated, at least.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why was Darth Vader crying after killing the Separatist Council?
Answer: Unlike what some answers suggest, it’s not because of what he just did. Anakin always hated the Separatist Council - they were the root of the years he and everyone he cared about spent in war. Killing them was just about the only positive thing that he’d be happy about. So then, why did Vader cry after killing them? Simple - he was reminiscing about everything that happened prior. Over the course of just hours, Vader had betrayed the entire Jedi Council, slaughtered everything he had held dear (the Jedi Order), and submitted himself to an enemy who was notorious for his lies. Vader was unstable - he had a plethora of emotions he was battling. Anger, fear, regret…all of it. Perhaps it was then that he came to terms with the gravity of the situation.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Knowhere the severed head of ego? It makes sense because ego is just a floating brain.
Answer: No. Knowhere is an ancient severed head of a celestial. This is what it looked like in Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 1: This was Ego years later in Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: Ego’s head was never severed, and his entire being (including his brain) was on his planet - the brain being at the core of the planet. Once the planet was destroyed, so was he. He really has nothing to do with whoever the Knowhere celestial is. This is all not to mention that, at least in the comics, Ego isn’t even a Celestial. The MCU hints at the idea that he is but never truly confirms it, but in the comics, Ego is just a big planet guy.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If MCU Thanos can easily break Vibranium, can the Hulk?
Answer: It was far from easy. Look back at Thanos’ fight against Cap: Cap, just seconds before, bullied Thanos for a solid few moments - it was the hardest Thanos was hit up until that point. The Mad Titan, at this moment, went on an angry rampage that took several extremely hard hits to eventually crack half of the sheild. This was, by no means, easy. This is, of course, the same Thanos who fairly easily wrecked Hulk all the way back in Infinity War: The Mad Titan put far less effort here than against Cap. While Hulk is strong, his hits didn’t do much to Thanos. The guy was merely playing with his food before demolishing it (hence Maw saying, “let him have his fun”). He was never in any remote danger, so it’s safe to say that Hulk’s hits were of no threat. So no - though he is quite strong, I don’t think Hulk would be able to break the most versatile substance on the planet.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How successful would Thanos be if he was a gladiator on Sakaar?
Answer: Well, remember Gladiator Hulk? The guy was unmatched on Sakaar for a long time, rising his way up to the top of the Gladiator food chain on the Grandmaster’s planet. He was completely unbeatable and had no foes who could stand a chance against him. There was even an entire planet-wide fanbase for him because of his unmatched strength. This is that same Hulk when he fought Thanos: The poor green man was completely outclassed, and Thanos didn’t even have to use an Infinity Stone once! The Mad Titan is in a whole different league of strength and skill, so rising the ranks in the Grandmaster’s fighting pits would be a breeze. Hell, he’d probably end up running the place after a while.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What minor event in the MCU would change everything if it didn't happen?
Answer: When Nick Fury decided to open a HYDRA file. All the way back in The Winter Soldier, there was a scene wear Nick Fury decided to, out of the blue, open the Lemurian Star’s satellite launch file. However, it was then that he realized there was a suspicious level of secrecy surrounding it. Fury knew damn well that he never revoked himself access from highly-confidential SHIELD files. It was this one moment that led to Fury ordering Director Pierce to delay Project Insight, and it subsequently led to his almost-successful assassination attempt. It was only because of the escalation that Fury alerted Cap that SHIELD was compromised. It was then that Steve (with the help of Sam, Nat, Maria, and everyone else he recruited) found out about HYDRA’s true intentions of murdering millions of people in order to further their agenda. So, how does this change “everything” in the MCU? Well, notice some of the names on the list of those to be eliminated: Tony Stark was one of the targets. Sitwell also confirms that Stephen Strange was one as well. These two names became more than just “powerful people” - they saved the universe as we know it.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are some major inconsistencies in the MCU that the average viewer doesn’t notice?
Answer: This one’s not really Marvel’s fault, but it is a major inconsistency that happens way often than you think: having the same actors. Here are just a few: Bucky claims to have read The Hobbit, which coincidentally featured Andy Serkis (Ulysses Klaue), Liv Tyler (Betty Ross), Karl Urban (Skurge), Cate Blanchett (Hela), and others as characters in the trilogy. Star Wars (which was confirmed to exist by Steve in The Winter Soldier) has a ton of familiar faces that I am definitely not going to individually list out. Hot Tub Time Machine (referenced in Endgame) also has a fairly familiar face. There are literally hundreds of other examples, but you get the point. Because many of the actors Marvel hires are a-listers, it’s impossible to not have any inconsistencies whenever they reference another big franchise. However, it does make for confusion as to how exactly this works in their universe.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why does The First Order seem so weak compared to the Empire?
Answer: This was the Empire at its peak: This was the First Order at its peak: Granted, you could make the case that the First Order had weaker leadership, but there is no way in hell that their raw power was less than the Empire. If anything, they were much more powerful than before. Did Palpatine accomplish more politically than Kylo ever could? Sure. But was Palpatine’s military “so weak compared to the Empire”? Absolutely not.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Which MCU character would win in a round of golf?
Answer: Hawkeye, by far. Clint’s precision is horrendously underrated. He’s able to shoot perfect targets behind his back and hit dead accurately. His physics game is on point. Though he may not be the strongest or the smartest, he’s sure as hell the most precise.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why doesn't Emperor Palpatine ever wear a crown?
Answer: Palpatine was never too keen on improving his personal appearance. Notice what he wears pretty much the entirety of his dictatorship: Not exactly the cover of a fashion magazine. Palpatine never wished for external appearances of power, he wished for true power. And he got it. He didn’t have to prove his authority to anybody, so the moment he became Emperor, he got rid of those tacky Chancellor outfits and stuck with the one thing in his closet. So in short, Palpatine never wears a crown because he has no need for one.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Can Jedi block bullets? If not, why? They can block blaster bolts.
Answer: Technically, yes. The Jedi have been shown to block bullets, but due to their small size and large quantity, they are far more difficult to block than a standard blaster. This begs the question: If it’s so much harder for Jedi to block bullets, why does almost everyone use blasters? The answer is simple: blasters are far cheaper to produce, and they have more rounds. They also have different levels of shot strength, depending on the situation. It also penetrates trooper’s armor much more effectively than bullets. And while it is true that fighting Jedi with blasters is a downside, the Galaxy with at least quintillions of people isn’t going to change their entire military method just for 10,000 guys in robes that they might happen to run into. Seeing a Jedi was so rare that many thought they were made up - Han Solo included.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What would happen if Fat Thor met Odin instead of Frigga?
Answer: I’m going to go out on a limb and say that things would actually turn worse. See, Frigga knew Thor and Loki better than anyone. And not only this, but she also had vision beyond the mortal realm. She tells Thor as much when she explains how she knows he is from another timeline: Odin, however, was different. He wasn’t a witch with foresight, and I’d reckon Frigga had a better relationship with them than he did (seeing as since the first Thor movie, Odin and his sons’ relationship have almost always been on more serious terms). And this is all not to mention that Odin is, by all accounts, wildly ignorant on occasion. Because of this, I don’t think he’d even figure out who Thor was. And even if he did, he would be more hostile/cautious of him more than happy. This would probably lead Thor to be more in a hurry to leave than anything else, and I’d imagine he’d keep his interaction(s) with his father brief.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why couldn’t Steve Rogers lift Mjölnir in Avengers: Age of Ultron?
Answer: He did. Notice again the little nudge Mjolnir makes when Cap tries lifting it: Thor saw it, and Cap definitely felt it. Mjolnir was confirmed to be pretty much immovable. Even with his strength, Cap has no way in hell to even slightly nudge the enchanted weapon if he wasn’t worthy. What actually happened was that Cap, at that moment, realized he was worthy - but he decided not to lift it completely so as to steal Thor’s thunder. The only time he did use it was when it was necessary. That selfless and honorable act alone just confirms he was worthy to wield it in the first place.

Name: Crantzer
Question: If Tony Stark was able to work in Wakanda, how much better would his technology have become?
Answer: It wouldn’t change as much as you think. By time time Infinity War rolled around, Tony’s tech (particularly his nanotech) was already far beyond what any other country could ever dream of making - including Wakanda. The suit was literally millennia ahead of its time and had near-magical properties like fatal wound healing, having enough durability to fend off an Infinity Stone, and making the Mad Titan himself bleed. The whole point that IW and Endgame had such advanced tech was that it was supposed to be the absolute pinnacle of innovation - it was Tony’s last suit. It’s highly unlikely (if not impossible) with Earth’s technology to further improve on what Tony managed to build. At best, perhaps Tony would be able to make some minor exterior modifications using vibranium to make it more durable. But even that wouldn’t make it much more powerful than it already is.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is the reason Captain America did not age like everyone else at the end of Marvel's Avengers: Infinity War?
Answer: Because of the super soldier serum. Remember Isaiah Bradley? Bradley said that he was injected with the super soldier serum in the 50s. Even if we assume that he was as young as 21 years old in the mid-50s, that would make Bradley at least 90 years old. The guy looks pretty spry for his age. Not counting the 70 years he was frozen, Cap was 35 by Endgame. He then went back in time from 1945 to 2023, so that’s another 78 years - making him 113. I’d say he looks pretty good for being triple digits.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why was Captain America able to pick up Thor's hammer in Avengers: Endgame but not earlier Avenger movies?
Answer: He actually could’ve lifted it whenever he wanted. Look back at this scene from Age of Ultron: Notice that little twitch Mjolnir made? Thor saw it, and Cap felt it. This was the moment Cap (and Thor) realized that he was worthy of lifting Mjolnir. The fact that it even slightly moved when it is clear that it is basically an immovable object already confirms that he was worthy. Cap just decided not to lift it to maintain Thor’s reputation, and he only used it again when it was necessary.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why do people like Tony Stark more when Captain America and Natasha Romanoff are ready to sacrifice themselves anytime, while Stark hesitated and was scared to sacrifice himself?
Answer: Because he had something to lose. Steve and Natasha were ready to sacrifice themselves - they always have been. They had no family, and the only people who truly cared about them were the friends they worked with. That’s not to mention that they were, at the time, illegal war criminals in almost every country. So a comfortable life isn’t something for them to look forward to. That’s where Tony was different. Unlike the others, Tony finally had what he never did - a purpose. He had family to take care of. Hell, he even had Peter to take care of. It’s unimaginably harder to make a decision that would affect all of them than when you’re on your own. Tony had fear of what would come, and rightfully so. But he didn’t let that stop him from making the sacrifice play, which saved the universe forever. That’s what makes Tony’s sacrifice the greatest in the MCU.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why is Kylo Ren's lightsaber ridiculous? Why doesn't he have a normal lightsaber?
Answer: First and foremost, it had a practical benefit. As you may already know, a Sith’s lightsaber is designed by bleeding their kyber crystal. It’s done by utilizing their anger and hatred. After destroying Luke’s rebuilt Jedi Temple, Ben bleeded his crystal. However, the crystal was cracked in the process. As a result, Ren modified his lightsaber by adding lateral vents to either side of the handle in order to divert the extra heat generated by the crystal. Secondly, it was already a design. Kylo’s crossguard design dates all the way back to the ancient lightsabers during the Great Scourge of Malachor. One famous example of someone with this design was Burryaga Agaburry, a Jedi in the High Republic era. It’s not like Kylo made up a new design, it had already been used by man Jedi and Sith in the past. He simply used it to make up for the crystal’s flaw.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What did Nebula from Marvel look like before she was not a cyborg?
Answer: It’s not too difficult to imagine. We know that Nebula is naturally blue, so throw in the comic-accurate blue hair, and voila.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How would Ebony Maw (MCU) fare against Darth Vader?
Answer: Not long. While it is true that they both share telekinesis, Maw has one weakness that Vader doesn’t: a lack of durability. Maw is very susceptible to damage and has taken it on a number of occasions. While he is good at diverting attacks, facing one head-on can kill him a lot like a human. Vader, on the other hand, is seen to be exponentially more durable: Combine this with the fact that Vader also boasts a number of other feats that Maw doesn’t (such as Force Choke, Force Push, and dueling skill), it’s clear that the Sith Lord would make quick work of Thanos’ child.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is Dr. Strange's best line in all the Marvel movies?
Answer: I’m surprised no one’s mentioned this: Probably the best line in the entire film, because it completely encompasses Strange’s character arc. Strange developed an underrated change of heart, and his selflessness was arguably greater than anyone else. With all the power that Strange had accumulated, he stood no chance against the beast that was Dormammu. But he didn’t let that stop him, and he decided to allow himself to suffer for eternity to save humanity. He’d die again and again (and even felt the pain each and every time), but he decided to continue for the sake of humanity. It’s honestly the greatest show of sacrifice in the entire MCU.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are the funny lines in the movie Avengers: Age Of Ultron?
Answer: Here are my personal favorites, in order: 5) “Never what?” 4) “Language!” 3) “Yay!” 2) “Actually, he’s the boss.” 1) “Elevator’s not worthy”

Name: Crantzer
Question: (Endgame Spoiler Alert) Why did Thanos’ beheading surprise so many Avengers fans?
Answer: Well, it came out of nowhere. The Avengers, at that moment, had Thanos where they wanted him - he had absolutely no power to “break free” or fight them off. Thus, the conversation was relatively relaxed. It was an interrogation of information that we as fans expected to get more of. But nope.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why didn't Tony just go back in time and stop Quill from punching Thanos?
Answer: Professor Hulk puts it well: Essentially, it boils down to this: Tony might’ve been able to save Peter’s universe by stopping him, but it’d do nothing to his own universe. Whatever change the Avengers made to other branches of time did not affect their own timeline - it simply affected the timeline they traveled to. The goal was to help their own timeline, not the timeline of others.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What minor event in the MCU would you say had the largest impact on everything that has happened up to this point?
Answer: When Tony decided to go through his dad’s old stuff. In Iron Man 2, Tony goes through his dad’s old junk and equations. While he does so, he plays videotapes of his dad in the background. Most of the videotapes were bloopers and intros to new designs, and he ignored most of it. However, one part of the videotape ended up being a message from Howard to Tony that he’d never seen before: Tony, you’re too young to understand this right now, so I thought I’d put it on film for you. I built this for you, and someday you’ll realize that it means a whole lot more than just people’s inventions - it represents my life’s work. This is the key to the future. I am limited by the technology of my time, but one day you’ll figure this out. And when you do, you will change the world. What is and always will be my greatest creation is you. This was what caused Tony to understand that there was more to hid dad’s blueprints than at first glance. And while doing a thorough investigation, he found that his dad left clues of an entirely new element! This element was what led Tony to cure his arc reactor poisoning. This seemingly minor moment of looking through Howard’s stuff changed everything. Tony had just months to live in Iron Man 2 prior to finding the cure. However, it was now that he knew how to fix it for good. It kept Tony alive to become the Iron Man we all know and love today. Without this decision Tony made, the universe would be in a completely different place.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is the darkest thing Luke Skywalker has ever done in the entire Star Wars franchise?
Answer: Probably when he joined forces with Palpatine. In the Expanded Universe, clues lead Luke to a secret chamber within the Imperial Palace. There, a vortex brought him to an Imperial Dungeon ship and face to face with an old enemy: Emperor Palpatine himself. The Sith Lord revealed that he had avoided death using Sith knowledge and cloning, and he tried to convince Luke to join him. With the intention of destroying the Dark Side from the inside, Luke decided to join Palpatine. Despite his initial plans, however, Luke’s naivety and inclination toward the dark side started to corrupt him from the inside. His aggressive efforts in sabotaging the Empire’s efforts fed his ego, and he could only watch as the Emperor blasted Leia with lightning in order to imprison her. It was only through Leia’s connection with the light side that eventually brought Luke back. Had she not been there, he would not have been able to resist aiding the Emperor’s plan to possess the body of Leia’s son.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Would Yoda be unstoppable if he was a Sith Lord?
Answer: Oh, yes. In Star Wars: Dark Rendevous, Yoda gives Dooku a glimpse of his potential power if he ever turned to the dark side (thus forbidding him from holding back): Whether it was the play of the holo-monitors, beaming their views of bleak space and distant battles, or some other trick of the light, Yoda's face was deeply hidden in the shadows, and for one terrible instant, he looked exactly like Darth Sidious. Or rather, it was Yoda as he might have been, or could yet become: a Yoda gone rotten, a Yoda whose awesome powers had been utterly unleashed by his connection to the dark side. In a flash, Dooku saw how foolish he had been, trying to urge the old Master to the dark side. If Yoda ever turned that way, Sidious himself would be annihilated. The universe had yet to comprehend the kind of evil that a Jedi Knight of nearly nine hundred years could wield. Yoda would annihilate quite literally any Force user who has ever existed (with the exception of the Mortis gods), putting him on a higher level of power than Luke, Vitiate, and Revan.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What are some things in Star Wars films you caught that you think others missed?
Answer: The Empire learned from its mistakes on Hoth. In The Last Jedi, we see Kylo and his army roll out with a fresh, upgraded platoon of AT-AT walkers. While there are a number of modifications, notice something particularly interesting: Extra leg Armor! This is a subtle hint to the Empire learning from their mistakes on Hoth, when they previously left the feet unguarded and thus allowed the rebels to destroy their fleet using speeders to trip them up with tow lines back in Empire Strikes Back.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What small detail from a movie do you love?
Answer: Here’s one you probably missed from The Avengers: Remember this scene? Well, shortly after this ordeal, you’ll notice a screen where Coulson is checking her and Clint’s records. See the coordinates up on the top left. Turns out they’re not just random. Looking it up, we find that they lead somewhere in Abidjan, West Africa. Now notice again what the record was called on Coulson’s screen: Abidjan Operation! This scene was shown for a split second, and yet Marvel’s production team was still on point. It’s truly amazing the attention to detail they put into even the tiniest of things.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What would happen if Magneto was part of the Avengers during Infinity War?
Answer: Well, for one, Thanos’ ship would be torn to pieces. Cull Obsidian wouldn’t last long once he loses his hammer. And, if it occurred, a fight between Thanos and Magneto would play out similarly to when he fought Wanda.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What if a child came up to Thanos and punched him?
Answer: “You’re a bold one, child…but I suggest using a bigger weapon next time.” He honestly wouldn’t do much - not in the MCU, at least. Thanos understood the value of someone who had great courage and natural strength - its why he picked out Gamora. He also wasn’t sadistic in the sense that he took pleasure in killing people for no reason. While he did unspeakable things, it was always with a goal in mind. In his own twisted way, Thanos did care about people in the sense that he made it his life’s purpose to provide them with more resources by eliminating half of all life. He was also a father of at least six children, so I doubt he liked hurting kids (other than in discipline like Nebula). Because of this, it’s highly unlikely he’d do anything more than just scaring the kid who punched him.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why was Order 66 ordered when it was?
Answer: It was perfect timing. Palpatine’s plan had almost completely come full circle. He had set this up for decades, and it all culminated into the perfect time to strike. By that time: Everything happened exactly as Palpatine had foreseen. There was nothing else to do but sit back and allow the Order to crumble from their own blindness, and make way for Palpatine’s absolute power.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is it actually obvious that Bruce Wayne is Batman?
Answer: Not at all. Bruce as a man put on a facade of being a billionaire playboy philanthropist. He was social, and he was your standard “Wall Street bro”. Batman, however, is a different person entirely. He was a no-nonsense criminal hunter who hunted down anyone who preyed on the innocent in Gotham, and the entire city feared his name. There’s no way in hell anyone would’ve been able to think that Bruce could ever even remotely be related to Batman. Of course, there’s also the more obvious factor - his disguise. Bruce covered most of his face when fighting crime, making it nearly impossible to identify him, even if you knew him. This is not to mention that he had a voice chance as well. Given his discreet and assassin-like secrecy as well as his personality change & face disguise, Bruce managed to fool everyone as to who he truly was. There’s really no possible way for someone to figure it out (which is something I’ve always had a problem with Lex being able to do in Batman v Superman). And besides, it’s much less obvious than Clark’s “secret identity”.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why didn't Luke Skywalker have children?
Answer: This was Luke’s living situation for the majority of his time after defeating the Empire: This was where he then spent his retirement: The guy hasn’t lived in the most urban areas. Luke has lived off-the-grid for nearly all of his life (in canon), and both planets had absolutely no other signs of human life. It’s highly unlikely he ever found a companion in his solace (besides, of course, the occasional Force ghost). And of course, no companion means no kids - unless you count the padawans he trained in his Jedi Temple.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is the exact reason that Jedi cannot get married?
Answer: While it is true that one reason for this was because the Order forbade attachments, there is another reason. The Force is often hereditary, meaning that if at least one parent was strong in the Force, chances are that the child would have aptitude in the Force as well. Thus, the concern of having a Force-sensitive family (especially with those unusually strong in the Force) is that they create an unending family dynasty of Force power, which could very likely lead to at least a few falling to the dark side and/or overthrowing the government because of their sheer power.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why does Thanos never touch the Time Stone in Infinity War?
Answer: All throughout the MCU, no one has ever touched the Time Stone (though other Infinity Stones have been touched). Notice how they’re some sort of barrier around it every time someone has the Time Stone in their hand: The Time Stone differs from the other stones in the sense that unlike all the others (reality, mind, power, space, and soul), time cannot be touched and/or felt. Thus, the Time Stone has a sort of barrier around it when a living person touches it. However, a simple inanimate object/machine has no problem touching it.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Which villains in the MCU would have the highest bounty?
Answer: While it is true that Thanos is the obvious answer and that people like Killmonger would have a high bounty because of their accomplishments, there is one MCU villain who is too often overlooked: Ronan. The guy was literally an intergalactic crusader hell-bent on the ancient Kree ideology that the entire universe should bend to their will. His name was involved in murdering countless from many different planets. He’s basically a watered-down Thanos, with none of the redeeming qualities. There would absolutely be many planets and even entire realms that would pay a hefty price for Ronan’s head. We see Xandar (one of Ronan’s targets) give Star-Lord and his crew total immunity and a high-end ship for protecting them against the guy. There would definitely be more than a few other planets who’d be happy to see him dead as well, and I’m sure many of them would pay hefty sums for it.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did the Celestials not try to prevent Thanos from wiping out half of all life in the universe in Infinity War?
Answer: It’s just lazy writing. Pre-Eternals, there is a solid explanation: The Celestials all died out or were idle (like the Grandmaster). And it makes sense - we saw Ego die, Knowhere was literally the severed head of a Celestial, and Esos was never seen after his first appearance in Guardians of the Galaxy. However, Eternals changed lore entirely. Now, we know that Celestials always have existed and are able to meddle in affairs if necessary (like when taking up the Eternals from Earth). And though they can’t meddle in human affairs, it certainly seems like intergalactic genocide would be reason enough to intervene. This is not to mention that this does affect the Celestials as well, seeing as the lack of organic material to consume (after the snap) would be bad for them. So no, there is no logical explanation why the Celestials didn’t intervene against Thanos.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why is it that Ventress never had the Sith eyes while other Siths did?
Answer: Because she wasn’t truly immersed in the dark side. Ventress and her “career” in the dark side was not your typical master-and-apprentice situation. Though she was an apprentice, she was more of an assassin for Count Dooku. That’s what she was officially, at least (in order to prevent suspicion from Palpatine that Dooku was plotting against him). Because of this, Dooku never truly taught Ventress about many Sith rituals and/or powers. He taught her as a Jedi would (lightsaber skill and connection to the Force), but he never actively trained her to hone in her anger and rage. Neither Ventress nor Dooku were ever overrun by the dark side. They were never consumed with anger/hate. Because of this, they never had the iconic yellow eyes that we see many Sith have.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why does Thanos respect Stark more than the other Avengers?
Answer: Because Thanos knew where true power lay - in the mind. Tony was a mere human being, a petty plaything to the Mad Titan. But through his genius and fearlessness, he managed to create a suit of armor around the world so powerful that it could bring gods to their knees. It’s hard to earn the respect of the Mad Titan - but Tony was one of those people.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How did Thor enter Wakanda during Infinity War when the shield around the country is supposedly still active?
Answer: Well, right before he went to Wakanda, Thor helped create Stormbreaker. And as Eitri pointed out, it theoretically had the power to summon the Bifrost. And thankfully, it did. Now as to the second part of the question, you’re right - Wakanda’s shield (at the top, at least) was active. But what makes the Bifrost so powerful is that it can go anywhere it wishes, and it breaks through nearly everything and anyone in its path. The Bifrost literally broke through vibranium.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why did Thanos choose the Chitauri as his preferred military and not the mindless Outriders?
Answer: Because quality soldiers are better than a lot of soldiers. The Outriders were, as you described, mindless. They were essentially ravaging beasts with no loyalties. They weren’t as intelligent or powerful as the Chitauri were. A lot of times, the military needs to do more than just attack. They need some sense of battle understanding, and Thanos got that with the Chitauri. That’s why he used it on Earth.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Can a Sith have morals?
