Answer: Contrary to popular belief, yes. We even see one in Legends: Darth Vectivus. Lumiya: “Darth Vectivus.” Jacen Solo: "Never heard of him." Lumiya: "That's because he did no evil. He didn't attempt to conquer the galaxy, try to wipe out the population of a star system or start an all-out war with the Jedi. He just existed, learned. Died of old age, surrounded by family and friends." (Legacy of the Force: Betrayal) Vectivus was an mining businessman who accidentally received power from a dark side nexus through a force-powered asteroid he was working on. He started experimenting with this new power of the dark side nexus. Eventually, Vectivus found a Sith, learned about the rules of the Sith, and became even stronger in the dark side. However, Vectivus continued to be a hard-headed businessman who had a keenly balanced sense of profit and fairness. That was, until his business of asteroid mining no longer became profitable and he closed shop. From then on, Vectivus went out into the Galaxy apprenticing himself, becoming more powerful, and eventually becoming a master himself. However, Vectivus never had any sort of confrontation with the Republic, fellow Sith, or even any Jedi. He only ever concerned himself with furthering the Sith’s knowledge and force abilities. And using his business-oriented mind, he failed to corrupt his mind like other Sith. Eventually, Vectivus died of natural causes alongside family and friends.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why isn't Flash (Barry Allen) as vengeful, angry, and resentful as Batman (Bruce Wayne), even though he lost his parents as well?
Answer: Two main reasons: 1) Barry still had a parent. This one’s probably the biggest reason Barry didn’t turn as Brue did. Barry had a dad whom he often met in prison and who gave him advice. They’d still talk, and they still had a relationship. This likely kept his humanity as much as it did. And even then, Barry was a loner who had very little friends - just like Bruce. The pain of losing a parent and the effects of that still affected him. 2) The murderers were different. Bruce’s parents met a horrifically traumatizing death where they were shot by deadbeats. And through it all, Bruce was helpless to save them. Because of this, Bruce decided to make it his life’s mission to hunt down criminals so that something like that would never happen again. Meanwhile, Barry’s incident was different. There was, as he remembers, a speedster that killed his mom. It was all a sudden, metaphysical, difficult-to-explain death that didn’t have anything to do with criminals (or anyone he could identify, for that matter).

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is something from the Marvel Universe that is really kind of dark, but gets ignored?
Answer: The Grandmaster’s world. Despite being a comedy movie, the whole concept of the Grandmaster’s “personal world” in Thor: Ragnarok is quite dark. It’s literal slavery where people are forced in gladiator-style fights, and countless people are slaughtered for enjoyment. And that’s all we know about him - there’s no telling what other stuff he’s done to people. It’s all brushed off as a joke, but it’s honestly it’s quite dark and quite a nightmare to live in.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Why is Hela stronger than Thor?
Answer: There are a few reasons for this: 1) She was the firstborn It was common in the Asgardian culture that most of the power goes to the firstborn. This was the case with Bor, whose firstborn was Odin (thus was the most powerful). So, it’s likely that Hela got the lion’s share of Odin’s powers. 2) She was much older For Asgardians, they grow more powerful the older they get. We see this in a non-canon fight between Thanos and Thor, where Thanos ages all the Avengers and weakens them - but Thor grows far more powerful and bullies Thanos, even with his stones. Hela was at least a few thousand years older than Thor. 3) She had a different mother While we don’t know exactly who Hela’s mother was in the MCU, we know for a fact it wasn’t Frigga. Because of this, it stands to reason that perhaps her mother was a powerful woman and maybe she inherited her power as well. Of course, that’s all speculation so I can’t say for sure. But it’s a theory.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is your favorite quote from Captain America: Civil War?
Answer: Zemo: My father lived outside the city, and I thought we would be safe there. My son was excited. He could see the Iron Man from the car window. I told my wife, "Don't worry. They're fighting in the city. We're miles from harm." And the dust cleared, and the screaming stopped…it took me two days until I found their bodies - my father still holding my wife and son in his arms. And the Avengers? They went home. I knew I couldn't kill them. More powerful men than me have tried. But if I could get them to kill each other... I'm sorry about your father. He seemed a good man, with a dutiful son. T'Challa: Vengeance has consumed you. It's consuming them. I'm done letting it consume me. Justice will come soon enough. Zemo: Tell that to the dead. This scene honestly broke me. You really cannot imagine the pain of losing a spouse or child unless you experience it yourself. Zemo was a man who had everything - but now, he has nothing to lose. And what’s worse, no one gives a damn. Props to Daniel Brühl for such a genuine and amazing portrayal.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Do Jedi get paid?
Answer: Technically, yes. Qui-Gon has quite a bit of Republic credits that he tells Watto he’s willing to spend. We also see Obi-Wan pay for a drink in AoTC. It’s clear that Jedi have some kind of money. However, it’s not an income. The Republic offers the Jedi something like stipends to use as they wish.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Is Abeloth considered to be the scariest of all Star Wars villains?
Answer: Yes. Abeloth had the power of both The Son and The Daughter (seeing as she drank from the Font of Power and bathed in the Pool of Knowledge). This made her far more powerful than any other being in existence. Her power level was so great that it took thousands of black holes to keep her under control. Even an EU Prime Luke Skywalker wasn’t even at a fraction of her power: It was no good. Abeloth had a dozen times the Force strength Luke had, and he could do no more than keep her from crushing his throat. (Fate of the Jedi: Vortex)

Name: Crantzer
Question: Could Luke Skywalker have defeated the Emperor?
Answer: Not in the Original Trilogy. “But Luke beat Vader! Surely he could stand a chance against the Emperor!” No. There are a number of factors you have to take into consideration. First, remember this? That’s what happened when Vader stopped toying around for one second. That’s what it led to. By the time of Return of the Jedi, Vader started becoming far more conflicted. He felt a pull of Anakin in him, so he didn’t even try most of the fight. In fact, half the fight was just him talking to Luke. Second, Luke showed up out of nowhere filled with tapping into the dark side for a second, which was what led to a power boost. Luke had, at most, a year of Force experience. He couldn’t stand a chance against the Sith Lord, even if he wanted to. That’s why it was so crucial for Vader to destroy Sidious - because he knew damn well Luke didn’t stand a chance by himself, and it was only Vader that could possibly take him on.

Name: Crantzer
Question: In the comics, have Odin and Dr. Strange met? Do they respect each other?
Answer: No, but they did in the MCU. Notice what Strange says to Thor in Thor: Ragnarok: Thor: “If you knew where [Odin] was, why didn’t you call me?” Dr. Strange: “I have to tell you, he was adamant that he not be disturbed. Your father said he’d chosen to remain in exile.” By this dialogue, we know for a fact that Strange and Odin did have some kind of interaction - however brief it may have been. There’s not enough to say for certain whether both parties respected each other, but it’s certainly likely.

Name: Crantzer
Question: How did Darth Vader know that Luke was his son?
Answer: From Boba Fett. After hearing of Luke’s existence (knowing that he was associated with Obi-Wan), Vader hired Boba Fett to hunt down him and bring him alive. So, Boba got to work. After violently interrogating his friends on Tatooine, Boba finds the identity of Luke. He then brought the information to Vader, who took it quite dramatically.

Name: Crantzer
Question: Are there any Jedi who can defeat Darth Vader in a 1v1 fight?
Answer: While it is true that people like Yoda and Obi-Wan could beat Vader, there is one lesser-known Jedi (in canon) who has been shown to completely outclass Vader in a fight: Kirak Infil’a. Infil’a was an absolute unit, and he was kicked out of the Order for his aggression. His power was far beyond the majority of those in the Jedi Temple. Vader was sent to hunt down rogue Jedi and obtain Kirak’s kyber crystal. However, that didn’t go as planned.

Name: Crantzer
Question: What is the funniest line in a Star Wars movie?
Answer: One of the funniest lines has gotta be Vader’s total dad joke to the overly ambitious Director Krennic in Rogue One: Vader has had a number of dark jokes in comics as well:
